title.zh: 卷七 魏書七 呂布臧洪傳
title.en: Volume 7: Book of Wei 7 - Biographies of Lü Bu and Zang Hong
title.raw: 卷七 魏書七 呂布臧洪傳 Volume 7: Book of Wei 7 - Biographies of Lü Bu and Zang Hong

sentences.zh: 呂布字奉先，五原郡九原人也。

translations.literal: Lü Bu, style name Fengxian, was a man of Jiuyuan in Wuyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu, whose courtesy name was Fengxian, came from Jiuyuan in Wuyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 以驍武給并州。

translations.literal: Because of his fierce martial skill he was assigned to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His prowess in arms earned him a post in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史丁原為騎都尉，屯河內，以布為主簿，大見親待。

translations.literal: The Inspector Ding Yuan was Colonel of Cavalry, stationed in Henei; he made Bu his chief clerk and showed him great favor and intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Ding Yuan served as Colonel of Cavalry with his army camped in Henei; he appointed Lü Bu chief clerk and treated him with conspicuous favor.

sentences.zh: 靈帝崩，原將兵詣洛陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling died, Yuan led troops to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ling's death, Ding Yuan marched his army to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：原字建陽。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Yuan's style name was Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes notes that Ding Yuan's courtesy name was Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 本出自寒家，為人粗略，有武勇，善騎射。

translations.literal: By origin he came from a poor household; in conduct he was rough, possessed martial courage, and was skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was born into a humble family, rough in manner but brave in battle and an excellent horseman and archer.

sentences.zh: 為南縣吏，受使不辭難，有警急，追寇虜，輒在其前。

translations.literal: As a clerk of the southern district, when given missions he did not shrink from hardship; when there was urgent alarm and pursuit of bandits, he was always in the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: As a clerk in the southern district he never flinched from a dangerous assignment; whenever bandits struck and had to be run down, he led the charge.

sentences.zh: 裁知書，少有吏用。〉

translations.literal: He barely knew letters and had little aptitude for clerical work.
translations.idiomatic: He barely knew how to read and had scant talent for administration.

sentences.zh: 與何進謀誅諸黃門，拜執金吾。

translations.literal: Together with He Jin he plotted to execute the palace eunuchs, and was appointed Bearer of the Mace.
translations.idiomatic: He joined He Jin's plot to slaughter the Yellow Gate eunuchs and was awarded the post of Bearer of the Golden Mace.

sentences.zh: 進敗，董卓入京都，將為亂，欲殺原，併其兵眾。

translations.literal: When Jin was defeated, Dong Zhuo entered the capital region; intending to cause turmoil, he wished to kill Yuan and annex his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When He Jin fell, Dong Zhuo marched into the capital. Planning to seize control, he meant to kill Ding Yuan and absorb his army.

sentences.zh: 卓以布見信於原，誘布令殺原。

translations.literal: Zhuo, because Bu was trusted by Yuan, enticed Bu to kill Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lü Bu enjoyed Ding Yuan's trust, Dong Zhuo suborned him to murder his patron.

sentences.zh: 布斬原首詣卓，卓以布為騎都尉，甚愛信之，誓為父子。

translations.literal: Bu cut off Yuan's head and presented it to Zhuo; Zhuo appointed Bu Colonel of Cavalry, greatly loved and trusted him, and swore a father-son bond.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu beheaded Ding Yuan and brought his head to Dong Zhuo, who named him Colonel of Cavalry, lavished favor on him, and pledged a pact like father and son.

sentences.zh: 布便弓馬，膂力過人，號為飛將。

translations.literal: Bu was adept at bow and horse; his strength surpassed others, and he was styled the Flying General.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu excelled as an archer and horseman and possessed extraordinary strength; men called him the Flying General.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至中郎將，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General of the Household and enfeoffed as marquis of Duting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to General of the Household and received the Duting village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 卓自以遇人無禮，恐人謀己，行止常以布自衛。

translations.literal: Zhuo himself, because he treated people rudely, feared that others would plot against him; in his movements he constantly used Bu as his bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo knew his bullying had made him enemies, so he kept Lü Bu at his side wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 然卓性剛而褊，忿不思難，嘗小失意，拔手戟擲布。

translations.literal: Yet Zhuo's nature was harsh and narrow; in anger he did not consider consequences. Once, over a slight vexation, he drew a hand halberd and hurled it at Bu.
translations.idiomatic: But Dong Zhuo was rigid and quick-tempered; one day a petty annoyance made him snatch up a short halberd and throw it at Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 布拳捷避之，

translations.literal: Bu, nimble with his fists, dodged it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu dodged nimbly.

sentences.zh: 〈詩曰：「無拳無勇，職為亂階。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: 'Without strength, without courage—this is the stairway to disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry runs: 'Without strength, without courage—it becomes the step to chaos.'

translations.literal: The commentary says: 'Quan means strength.'
translations.idiomatic: The gloss explains quan as 'strength.'

sentences.zh: 為卓顧謝，卓意亦解。

translations.literal: He turned and apologized to Zhuo, and Zhuo's mood also eased.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu turned back and apologized, and Dong Zhuo's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 由是陰怨卓。

translations.literal: From this he secretly harbored resentment toward Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment Lü Bu nursed a secret grudge against Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓常使布守中閤，布與卓侍婢私通，恐事發覺，心不自安。

translations.literal: Zhuo often had Bu guard the inner chambers; Bu carried on secretly with one of Zhuo's maidservants, feared discovery, and was inwardly uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo habitually posted Lü Bu to guard the inner apartments, where Lü Bu began an affair with one of Zhuo's maids; dreading exposure, he lived in constant anxiety.

sentences.zh: 先是，司徒王允以布州里壯健，厚接納之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Minister of Education Wang Yun, because Bu was robust and from the same province and district, received him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Yun had already taken a liking to Lü Bu—another sturdy northerner—and welcomed him warmly.

sentences.zh: 後布詣允，陳卓幾見殺狀。

translations.literal: Later Bu went to Yun and described how Zhuo had nearly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü Bu sought Wang Yun out and told him how Dong Zhuo had almost murdered him.

sentences.zh: 時允與僕射士孫瑞密謀誅卓，是以告布使為內應。

translations.literal: At that time Yun and Deputy Director Shisun Rui were secretly plotting to kill Zhuo; therefore he informed Bu to act as an inside respondent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun was already plotting Dong Zhuo's assassination with Deputy Director Shisun Rui, so he enlisted Lü Bu as his agent inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 布曰：「奈如父子何！

translations.literal: Bu said: 'What about being like father and son!'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu protested, 'But we swore an oath like father and son!'

sentences.zh: 」允曰：「君自姓呂，本非骨肉。

translations.literal: Yun said: 'Your surname is Lü by origin; you are not bone and flesh.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun replied, 'Your surname is Lü—you were never his kin.'

sentences.zh: 今憂死不暇，何謂父子？

translations.literal: Now you have no leisure even to worry about death—what talk of father and son?
translations.idiomatic: You are fighting for your life—what kind of father and son bond is that?'

sentences.zh: 」布遂許之，手刃刺卓。

translations.literal: Bu then consented and personally stabbed Zhuo with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu agreed and ran Dong Zhuo through with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 語在卓傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Zhuo's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full story appears in Dong Zhuo's biography.

sentences.zh: 允以布為

translations.literal: Yun appointed Bu as
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun appointed Lü Bu

sentences.zh: （奮威）

translations.literal: (General Who Displays Might)
translations.idiomatic: (General Who Displays Might)

sentences.zh: 〔奮武〕將軍，假節，儀比三司，進封溫侯，共秉朝政。

translations.literal: [General Who Displays Martial Power], granted credentials of authority, ceremonial rank equal to the Three Dukes, advanced enfeoffment as marquis of Wen, and together they held court government.
translations.idiomatic: [General Who Displays Martial Power], with imperial credentials and ceremonial standing equal to the Three Excellencies, promoted to Marquis of Wen: together they governed the court.

sentences.zh: 布自殺卓後，畏惡涼州人，涼州人皆怨。

translations.literal: After Bu killed Zhuo, he feared and loathed the men of Liangzhou, and the men of Liangzhou all harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After Dong Zhuo's death Lü Bu despised and feared the Liangzhou troops, and they hated him in return.

sentences.zh: 由是李傕等遂相結還攻長安城。

translations.literal: Therefore Li Jue and others then banded together and returned to attack Chang'an city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his allies therefore united and marched back to storm Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：郭汜在城北。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Guo Si was north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes places Guo Si north of the walls.

sentences.zh: 布開城門，將兵就汜，言「且卻兵，但身決勝負」。

translations.literal: Bu opened the city gate, led troops toward Si, and said, 'For now withdraw the troops; let us two alone decide victory or defeat.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu opened the gates, rode out to face Guo Si, and proposed a duel: 'Pull your men back—let you and I settle this alone.'

sentences.zh: 汜、布乃獨共對戰，布以矛刺中汜，汜後騎遂前救汜，汜、布遂各兩罷。〉

translations.literal: Si and Bu then fought face to face alone; Bu pierced Si with a spear; Si's rear cavalry then advanced to rescue Si; Si and Bu thereupon each withdrew on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The two men fought alone until Lü Bu speared Guo Si; Guo's escort then rushed up and pulled him clear, and both sides broke off the fight.

sentences.zh: 布不能拒，傕等遂入長安。

translations.literal: Bu could not resist, and Jue and others thereupon entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu could not hold them, and Li Jue's host poured into the capital.

sentences.zh: 卓死後六旬，布亦敗。

translations.literal: Six decad-days after Zhuo's death, Bu also was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty days after Dong Zhuo's death, Lü Bu too was beaten.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案《英雄記》曰：諸書，布以四月二十三日殺卓，六月一日敗走，時又無閏，不及六旬。〉

translations.literal: Your subject Song Zhi, examining the Yingxiong ji, says: In various books Bu killed Zhuo on the twenty-third day of the fourth month and fled in defeat on the first day of the sixth month; at that time there was likewise no intercalary month, so it does not reach six decad-days.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: other texts date Zhuo's death to the twenty-third of the fourth month and Lü Bu's flight to the first of the sixth—with no leap month that year, so 'six decad-days' does not quite fit.

sentences.zh: 將數百騎出武關，欲詣袁術。

translations.literal: Leading several hundred riders he exited Wuguan Pass, intending to go to Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He escaped through Wuguan with a few hundred horsemen, heading for Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 布自以殺卓為術報讎，欲以德之。

translations.literal: Bu himself thought that by killing Zhuo he had avenged Shu, and wished to bind Shu with obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu assumed that slaying Dong Zhuo had settled Yuan Shu's blood feud and hoped to win his gratitude.

sentences.zh: 術惡其反覆，拒而不受。

translations.literal: Shu detested his inconstancy and refused him, not accepting him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu despised his fickle loyalty and turned him away.

sentences.zh: 北詣袁紹，紹與布擊張燕于常山。

translations.literal: He went north to Yuan Shao; Shao together with Bu attacked Zhang Yan in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He rode north to Yuan Shao, who joined him in a campaign against Zhang Yan in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 燕精兵萬餘，騎數千。

translations.literal: Yan had crack troops over ten thousand and several thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan commanded more than ten thousand elite soldiers and several thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 布有良馬曰赤兔。

translations.literal: Bu had a fine horse called Red Hare.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu rode a celebrated charger named Red Hare.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：時人語曰：「人中有呂布，馬中有赤兔。」〉

translations.literal: The Cao Man zhuan says: People of the time said: 'Among men there is Lü Bu; among horses there is Red Hare.'
translations.idiomatic: The unofficial History of Cao Cao quotes a contemporary saying: 'Lü Bu among men, Red Hare among horses.'

sentences.zh: 常與其親近成廉、魏越等陷鋒突陳，遂破燕軍。

translations.literal: He constantly with his intimates Cheng Lian, Wei Yue, and others pierced the vanguard and broke formations, and thereby defeated Yan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again he charged the enemy line with Cheng Lian, Wei Yue, and his other trusted followers, shattering Zhang Yan's host.

sentences.zh: 而求益兵眾，將士鈔掠，紹患忌之。

translations.literal: Yet he sought more troops and masses; his officers and soldiers plundered; Shao worried about and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: But he kept demanding reinforcements while his men looted the countryside, until Yuan Shao grew anxious and suspicious.

sentences.zh: 布覺其意，從紹求去。

translations.literal: Bu perceived his intent and asked leave of Shao to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the mood, Lü Bu asked Yuan Shao's permission to leave.

sentences.zh: 紹恐還為己害，遣壯士夜掩殺布，不獲。

translations.literal: Shao feared he would become a harm to himself if he returned, and sent stalwart men by night to surprise and kill Bu; they did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao feared Lü Bu might one day turn on him and sent assassins to strike by night; they failed.

sentences.zh: 事露，布走河內，

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Bu fled to Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked, Lü Bu bolted for Henei.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：布自以有功於袁氏，輕傲紹下諸將，以為擅相署置，不足貴也。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Bu himself thought he had merit toward the Yuan clan, looked down on and was arrogant toward Shao's subordinate generals, and considered that they had presumptuously appointed and installed one another, not worth esteeming.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes adds that Lü Bu considered himself the Yuan family's benefactor, sneered at Yuan Shao's officers, and dismissed their self-made appointments as beneath notice.

sentences.zh: 布求還洛，紹假布領司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Bu requested to return to Luoyang; Shao provisionally had Bu act as Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu asked permission to return west; Yuan Shao made him acting Colonel Director of Retainers.

sentences.zh: 外言當遣，內欲殺布。

translations.literal: Outwardly he said he would send him off; inwardly he wished to kill Bu.
translations.idiomatic: He talked of seeing Lü Bu off while planning his murder.

sentences.zh: 明日當發，紹遣甲士三十人，辭以送布。

translations.literal: The next day when he was about to depart, Shao sent thirty armored soldiers on the pretext of escorting Bu.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning of Lü Bu's departure Yuan Shao assigned thirty armored men 'to see him on his way.'

sentences.zh: 布使止於帳側，偽使人於帳中鼓箏。

translations.literal: Bu had them stop by the side of the tent; falsely he had someone in the tent pluck the zither.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu had them wait outside his tent while a servant strummed a zither within—an empty show of occupation.

sentences.zh: 紹兵臥，布無何出帳去，而兵不覺。

translations.literal: Shao's soldiers lay down; before long Bu exited the tent and departed, and the soldiers did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: The escort fell asleep; Lü Bu slipped out unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 夜半兵起，亂斫布床被，謂為已死。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night the soldiers rose and wildly hacked Bu's bed and bedding, thinking he was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they attacked the bed in a frenzy, certain they had killed him.

sentences.zh: 明日，紹訊問，知布尚在，乃閉城門。

translations.literal: The next day Shao inquired and questioned, learned Bu was still alive, and thereupon closed the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning Yuan Shao learned Lü Bu was still alive and ordered the gates shut.

sentences.zh: 布遂引去。〉

translations.literal: Bu thereupon led his force away.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was already gone.

sentences.zh: 與張楊合。

translations.literal: He joined with Zhang Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Zhang Yang.

sentences.zh: 紹令眾追之，皆畏布，莫敢逼近者。

translations.literal: Shao ordered the host to pursue him; all feared Bu, and none dared draw near.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao ordered pursuit, but no one dared close with the Flying General.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：楊及部曲諸將，皆受傕、汜購募，共圖布。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Yang and the generals of his personal troops all received offers of reward from Jue and Si to join in plotting Bu.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes reports that Li Jue and Guo Si had put a price on Lü Bu's head and won over Zhang Yang's officers.

sentences.zh: 布聞之，謂楊曰：「布，卿州里也。

translations.literal: When Bu heard it, he said to Yang: 'Bu is of your province and district.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu warned Zhang Yang, 'We hail from the same commandery.'

sentences.zh: 卿殺布，於卿弱。

translations.literal: If you kill Bu, for you it is weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Killing me would only weaken you.'

sentences.zh: 不如賣布，可極得汜、傕爵寵。

translations.literal: It is better to sell out Bu; you can to the utmost obtain rank and favor from Si and Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hand me over and collect the full reward from Guo Si and Li Jue.'

sentences.zh: 」楊於是外許汜、傕，內實保護布。

translations.literal: Yang thereupon outwardly promised Si and Jue, but inwardly in truth protected Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang feigned cooperation with Guo Si and Li Jue while sheltering Lü Bu in fact.

sentences.zh: 汜、傕患之，更下大封詔書，以布為潁川太守。〉

translations.literal: Si and Jue were troubled by it; they again issued a grandly sealed edict, appointing Bu as Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Annoyed, Guo Si and Li Jue countered with an imperial rescript sealed in the great envelope, naming Lü Bu administrator of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 張邈字孟卓，東平壽張人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Miao, style name Mengzhuo, was a man of Shouzhang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao, courtesy name Mengzhuo, was a native of Shouzhang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 少以俠聞，振窮救急，傾家無愛，士多歸之。

translations.literal: In youth he was renowned for knight-errantry; he raised the destitute and rescued the urgent, poured out his household without stint, and many men attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he made a name as a chivalrous figure—always helping the needy at his own expense—so bold spirits flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 太祖、袁紹皆與邈友。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor and Yuan Shao were both friends with Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Both Cao Cao and Yuan Shao counted him as a friend.

sentences.zh: 辟公府，以高第拜騎都尉，遷陳留太守。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Excellencies' offices; with high ranking he was appointed Colonel of Cavalry and transferred to Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital service, he graduated with honors, received the colonelcy of cavalry, and rose to administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 董卓之亂，太祖與邈首舉義兵。

translations.literal: At Dong Zhuo's turmoil, Grand Progenitor together with Miao first raised righteous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo seized power, Cao Cao and Zhang Miao were among the first to raise armies against him.

sentences.zh: 汴水之戰，邈遣衞茲將兵隨太祖。

translations.literal: At the battle of the Bian River, Miao sent Wei Zi to lead troops following Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bian River Zhang Miao detached Wei Zi's contingent to fight under Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 袁紹旣爲盟主，有驕矜色，邈正議責紹。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao had become alliance chief, he had a proud and arrogant demeanor; Miao with upright discourse reproached Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan Shao headed the coalition his manner turned arrogant; Zhang Miao rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 紹使太祖殺邈，太祖不聽，責紹曰：「孟卓，親友也，是非當容之。

translations.literal: Shao had Grand Progenitor kill Miao; Grand Progenitor did not listen, and reproached Shao, saying: 'Mengzhuo is a kinsman friend; right and wrong ought to be tolerated in him.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao told Cao Cao to execute Zhang Miao; Cao refused. 'Mengzhuo is family to me,' he told Yuan Shao. 'You must allow him his faults.'

sentences.zh: 今天下未定，不宜自相危也。

translations.literal: Now the realm is not yet settled; it is not appropriate that we endanger one another among ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is still unsettled—we cannot afford to turn on each other.

sentences.zh: 」邈知之，益德太祖。

translations.literal: When Miao knew of it, he the more valued Grand Progenitor in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Zhang Miao, he felt even deeper gratitude toward Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖之征陶謙，勑家曰：「我若不還，往依孟卓。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor campaigned against Tao Qian, he instructed his household, saying: 'If I do not return, go rely on Mengzhuo.'
translations.idiomatic: Before marching against Tao Qian, Cao Cao told his family: 'If I do not come back, seek refuge with Mengzhuo.'

sentences.zh: 」後還，見邈，垂泣相對。

translations.literal: Later he returned, saw Miao, and wept face to face.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he and Zhang Miao wept in each other's arms.

sentences.zh: 其親如此。

translations.literal: Their intimacy was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the closeness between them.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：布見備，甚敬之，謂備曰：「我與卿同邊地人也。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: When Bu saw Bei, he greatly respected him, and said to Bei: 'I and you are both men of the borderlands.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes quotes Lü Bu's first meeting with Liu Bei: 'We are both men of the northern frontier,' he said with great respect.

sentences.zh: 布見關東起兵，欲誅董卓。

translations.literal: Bu saw the armies east of the pass arise and wished to execute Dong Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: I watched the lords east of the mountains take up arms against Dong Zhuo.'

sentences.zh: 布殺卓東出，關東諸將無安布者，皆欲殺布耳。

translations.literal: Bu killed Zhuo and went out east; among the generals east of the pass there was none who was at peace with Bu; all wished to kill Bu only.
translations.idiomatic: I killed Dong Zhuo and came east, yet not one of those generals will have me—they all want me dead.'

sentences.zh: 」請備於帳中坐婦牀上，令婦向拜，酌酒飲食，名備爲弟。

translations.literal: He invited Bei to sit in the tent on a woman's bed, had the woman face and bow, poured wine and feasted, and called Bei 'younger brother.'
translations.idiomatic: He brought Liu Bei into his tent, seated him on the women's couch, had his wife pay her respects, poured the wine, and called him 'younger brother.'

sentences.zh: 備見布語言無常，外然之而內不說。〉

translations.literal: Bei saw that Bu's words were inconstant; outwardly he assented, but inwardly he was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei noted Lü Bu's erratic talk and nodded along while inwardly disliking him.

sentences.zh: 邈從布，留超將家屬屯雍丘。

translations.literal: Miao followed Bu, leaving Chao to lead dependents and garrison Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao threw in his lot with Lü Bu and left Zhang Chao to hold Yongqiu with the families.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻圍數月，屠之，斬超及其家。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor attacked and besieged for several months, slaughtered it, and executed Chao together with his household.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao besieged the city for months, sacked it, and put Zhang Chao and his family to the sword.

sentences.zh: 邈詣袁術請救未至，自爲其兵所殺。

translations.literal: Miao went to Yuan Shu to beg rescue; before it arrived, he was killed by his own troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao rode to Yuan Shu for help but was murdered by his own men before relief arrived.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝春秋》曰：袁術議稱尊號，邈謂術曰：「漢據火德，絕而復揚，德澤豐流，誕生明公。

translations.literal: The Xiandi Chunqiu says: When Yuan Shu deliberated assuming the honored title, Miao said to Shu: 'Han occupies the virtue of Fire; though cut off, it again rises; virtuous grace flows rich, and the enlightened lord was born.'
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Xian record Yuan Shu's bid for the throne. Zhang Miao told him: 'The Han holds the virtue of Fire—it falters, then flares again; its blessings spread wide, and they produced a man like you.'

sentences.zh: 公居軸處中，入則享于上席，出則爲衆目之所屬，華、霍不能增其高，淵泉不能同其量，可謂巍巍蕩蕩，無與爲貳。

translations.literal: You dwell at the axle and center; within you enjoy the upper seat; without you are what the throng of eyes attaches to; Hua and Huo cannot increase your height; deep springs cannot equal your measure; one may call it towering and vast, without a second.'
translations.idiomatic: You stand at the pivot—honored at court, the cynosure of every gaze; neither Mount Hua nor Mount Huo could make you higher, nor any abyss match your depth—magnificent, unrivaled.'

sentences.zh: 何爲捨此而欲稱制？

translations.literal: Why discard this and wish to assume the imperial style?
translations.idiomatic: Why cast that aside to proclaim yourself emperor?'

sentences.zh: 恐福不盈眥，禍將溢世。

translations.literal: I fear fortune will not fill the corner of the eye, and calamity will overflow the age.
translations.idiomatic: Your blessing may never reach the width of an eye's corner; disaster could flood the age.'

sentences.zh: 莊周之稱郊祭犧牛，養飼經年，衣以文繡，宰執鸞刀，以入廟門，當此之時，求爲孤犢不可得也！

translations.literal: Zhuang Zhou told of the suburban-sacrifice ox: fed for a full year, clothed in patterned embroidery, the butcher grasping the phoenix knife and entering the temple gate—at that moment, to seek to be a lone calf is not possible!'
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi's ox fattened for the suburban rites—fed for a year, draped in brocade, led with the ritual knife through the temple gate—at that point not even a solitary calf's life is within reach!'

sentences.zh: 」案本傳，邈詣術，未至而死。

translations.literal: Examining the main biography, Miao went to Shu but before arriving died.
translations.idiomatic: The main text, however, says Zhang Miao died on the road before he reached Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 而此云諫稱尊號，未詳孰是。〉

translations.literal: Yet this says he remonstrated against assuming the honored title; it is not detailed which is correct.
translations.idiomatic: This passage makes him Yuan Shu's critic—Pei Songzhi cannot say which version is right.

sentences.zh: 術欲結布爲援，乃爲子索布女，布許之。

translations.literal: Shu wished to ally Bu as support; therefore for his son sought Bu's daughter, and Bu consented.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu sought Lü Bu as an ally and asked for Lü's daughter for his son; Lü Bu agreed.

sentences.zh: 術遣使韓胤以僭號議告布，并求迎婦。

translations.literal: Shu sent envoy Han Yin to inform Bu of the deliberation on usurping the title, and also requested to welcome the bride.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Han Yin to brief Lü Bu on his plan to claim the throne and to escort the bride home.

sentences.zh: 沛相陳珪恐術、布成婚，則徐、揚合從，將爲國難，於是往說布曰：「曹公奉迎天子，輔讚國政，威靈命世，將征四海，將軍宜與恊同策謀，圖太山之安。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of Pei, Chen Gui, feared that if Shu and Bu completed their marriage, Xu and Yang would form an allied league and would become a crisis for the state; thereupon he went to persuade Bu, saying: "Lord Cao has welcomed the Son of Heaven, assists and extols the administration of the state, his numinous might commands the age, and he will campaign across the four seas—the General ought to join him in common planning and seek the security of Mount Tai."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui, chancellor of Pei, feared a wedding between Yuan Shu and Lü Bu would weld Xu and Yang into an alliance and spell disaster for the court. He went to Lü Bu and urged him: Lord Cao has received the emperor, backs the government, and wields authority enough to conquer the realm; you should align with him and aim for stability as immovable as Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 今與術結婚，受天下不義之名，必有累卵之危。

translations.literal: Now if you ally by marriage with Shu, you will bear throughout the realm the name of unrighteousness, and will surely have the danger of eggs stacked high.
translations.idiomatic: If you marry into Yuan Shu's house now, you earn the empire's contempt as a traitor and court ruin like a pile of eggs ready to topple.

sentences.zh: 」布亦怨術初不己受也，女已在塗，追還絕婚，械送韓胤，梟首許市。

translations.literal: Bu also resented that Shu had at first not accepted him; the daughter was already on the road—he recalled her and broke off the marriage, sent Han Yin in fetters, and displayed his head in the market at Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu still smarted at Yuan Shu's earlier refusal of him. His daughter was already on the road when he called her back, annulled the match, bound Han Yin in chains for delivery, and exposed Han's head in the marketplace at Xu.

sentences.zh: 珪欲使子登詣太祖，布不肯遣。

translations.literal: Gui wished to send his son Deng to Grand Progenitor; Bu was unwilling to send him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui wanted to send his son Deng to Cao Cao, but Lü Bu would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 會使者至，拜布左將軍。

translations.literal: When an envoy arrived, Bu was appointed General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial envoy soon arrived and invested Lü Bu as General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 布大喜，即聽登往，并令奉章謝恩。

translations.literal: Bu was greatly pleased, immediately allowed Deng to go, and also ordered him to present a memorial thanking for grace.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was delighted and at once let Deng go, instructing him to submit a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：初，天子在河東，有手筆版書召布來迎。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: At first the Son of Heaven was east of the River; there was a personally brushed tablet summons summoning Bu to come welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes states that while the emperor was east of the Yellow River, he issued a handwritten summons on wooden slips inviting Lü Bu to escort him.

sentences.zh: 布軍無畜積，不能自致，遣使上書。

translations.literal: Bu's army had no stored provisions and could not get there of itself; he sent an envoy to submit a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's camp lacked supplies to make the journey, so he sent a memorial instead.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以布爲平東將軍，封平陶侯。

translations.literal: The court appointed Bu General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed him as marquis of Pingtao.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Pingtao.

sentences.zh: 使人於山陽界亡失文字，太祖又手書厚加慰勞布，說起迎天子，當平定天下意，并詔書購捕公孫瓚、袁術、韓暹、楊奉等。

translations.literal: The envoy lost the writing at the border of Shanyang; Grand Progenitor again personally wrote to lavishly console Bu, explaining the intent of welcoming the Son of Heaven and bringing peace to the realm, together with an edict offering rewards for the capture of Gongsun Zan, Yuan Shu, Han Xian, Yang Feng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The courier lost the documents in Shanyang; Cao Cao wrote again to reassure Lü Bu, spelled out the plan to welcome the emperor and pacify the empire, and enclosed arrest warrants for Gongsun Zan, Yuan Shu, Han Xian, Yang Feng, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 布大喜，復遣使上書於天子曰：「臣本當迎大駕，知曹操忠孝，奉迎都許。

translations.literal: Bu was greatly pleased and again sent an envoy to submit a memorial to the Son of Heaven, saying: 'Your subject originally ought to have welcomed the Great Carriage; learning that Cao Cao was loyal and filial, he welcomed and established the capital at Xu.'
translations.idiomatic: Overjoyed, Lü Bu sent another memorial to the throne: 'I meant to escort Your Majesty myself; learning that Cao Cao is loyal and has settled you at Xu,'

sentences.zh: 臣前與操交兵，今操保傅陛下，臣爲外將，欲以兵自隨，恐有嫌疑，是以待罪徐州，進退未敢自寧。

translations.literal: 'Your subject formerly crossed arms with Cao; now Cao guards and tutors Your Majesty, and your subject is a general outside; wishing to bring troops to attend himself, he feared suspicion would arise—therefore he awaits punishment at Xu Province and in advancing or retreating does not dare find peace.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I once fought Cao Cao; now that he attends you as regent, my bringing an army to court might look suspicious, so I remain at Xu Province uneasy in every move I make.'

sentences.zh: 」答太祖曰：「布獲罪之人，分爲誅首，手命慰勞，厚見褒獎。

translations.literal: He answered Grand Progenitor: 'Bu is a man who incurred guilt and by rights ought to be chief among those executed; your personal order consoles and favors me, and I am greatly seen with praise and reward.'
translations.idiomatic: To Cao Cao he wrote: 'I am a condemned man fit only for execution; your letter lifts me with undeserved praise.'

sentences.zh: 重見購捕袁術等詔書，布當以命爲效。

translations.literal: Again seeing the edict offering rewards for the capture of Yuan Shu and others, Bu ought to devote his life to effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the arrest warrant for Yuan Shu and company again, I will prove my loyalty with deeds.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖更遣奉車都尉王則爲使者，齎詔書，又封平東將軍印綬來拜布。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor further sent Bearer of the Coachman's Seal Wang Ze as envoy, bearing the edict, and also sealed the seal-cord of General Who Pacifies the East and came to invest Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then dispatched Wang Ze with the imperial edict and investiture regalia for General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 太祖又手書與布曰：「山陽屯送將軍所失大封，國家無好金，孤自取家好金更相爲作印，國家無紫綬，自取所帶紫綬以籍心。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor also personally wrote to Bu, saying: 'The Shanyang garrison delivered the great sealed matter that the General lost; the state has no fine gold—I personally took fine gold from my household and had another seal made for you; the state has no purple cord—I took the purple cord I wear and use it to express my heart.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao added a personal note: 'The packet you lost was recovered in Shanyang. Treasury gold was poor, so I supplied gold from my own house for your seal; there was no purple ribbon at court, so I sent the one from my belt to show my regard.'

sentences.zh: 將軍所使不良。

translations.literal: The agents the General employed were not good.
translations.idiomatic: Your messengers did not serve you well.'

sentences.zh: 袁術稱天子，將軍止之，而使不通章。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu styled himself Son of Heaven; the General stopped him, yet caused memorials not to go through.
translations.idiomatic: You checked Yuan Shu when he proclaimed himself emperor, yet blocked his memorials from reaching the throne.'

sentences.zh: 朝廷信將軍，使復重上，以相明忠誠。

translations.literal: The court trusts the General and had you submit again to clarify loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The court trusts you and asked you to petition again to prove your loyalty.'

sentences.zh: 」布乃遣登奉章謝恩，并以一好綬答太祖。〉

translations.literal: Bu thereupon sent Deng to present a memorial thanking for grace, and also with one fine cord answered Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu therefore had Deng deliver his thanks and returned a fine ribbon to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 登見太祖，因陳布勇而無計，輕於去就，宜早圖之。

translations.literal: When Deng saw Grand Progenitor, he therefore stated that Bu was brave but without stratagem, fickle in stay or go, and ought to be planned against early.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Deng met Cao Cao, he explained that Lü Bu was bold but unstrategic, quick to change sides, and should be dealt with soon.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「布，狼子野心，誠難久養，非卿莫能究其情也。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: 'Bu—wolf cub's wild heart—truly hard to nurture long; if not you, none can fathom his situation.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied, 'Lü Bu has the heart of a wolf cub—impossible to keep tame for long. Only you could read him so clearly.'

sentences.zh: 」即增珪秩中二千石，拜登廣陵太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gui's salary grade was increased to two thousand piculs at the central rate, and Deng was appointed Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Chen Gui's stipend to two thousand piculs and named Chen Deng administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 臨別，太祖執登手曰：「東方之事便以相付。

translations.literal: At parting, Grand Progenitor grasped Deng's hand and said: 'The affairs of the east I thus entrust to you.'
translations.idiomatic: As Chen Deng took his leave, Cao Cao clasped his hand. 'The entire east—I leave it in yours.'

sentences.zh: 」令登陰合部衆以爲內應。

translations.literal: He ordered Deng secretly to unite the troops and masses to act as inside respondent.
translations.idiomatic: He told Chen Deng to rally allies secretly as fifth columnists.

sentences.zh: 始，布因登求徐州牧，登還，布怒，拔戟斫机曰：「卿父勸吾恊同曹公，絕婚公路；

translations.literal: At first Bu through Deng requested the governorship of Xu Province; when Deng returned, Bu was angry, drew a halberd and hacked the bench, saying: 'Your father urged me to join with Lord Cao and break marriage with Gonglu;'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu had asked Chen Deng to secure him the governorship of Xu. When Deng came back empty-handed, Lü Bu seized a halberd and smashed his bench. 'Your father told me to side with Cao Cao and cut ties with Yuan Shu—'

sentences.zh: 今吾所求無一獲，而卿父子並顯重，爲卿所賣耳！

translations.literal: 'Now not one thing I sought was obtained, yet you father and son together are prominent and weighty—I have been sold by you!'
translations.idiomatic: '—yet I gained nothing while you two rose to honor—you have betrayed me!'

sentences.zh: 卿爲吾言，其說云何？

translations.literal: 'You spoke for me—what explanation is there?'
translations.idiomatic: 'What excuse do you offer?'

sentences.zh: 」登不爲動容，徐喻之曰：「登見曹公言：『待將軍譬如養虎，當飽其肉，不飽則將噬人。

translations.literal: Deng did not change demeanor, and slowly explained to him, saying: 'Deng saw Lord Cao and said: "Treating the General is like raising a tiger—one ought to fill it with meat; if not full it will bite people."'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng showed no fear and answered calmly: 'I told Cao Cao that managing you is like keeping a tiger—you must feed it meat or it will turn on its keeper.'

sentences.zh: 』公曰：『不如卿言也。

translations.literal: The lord said: "It is not as you say."
translations.idiomatic: He replied that your analogy missed the mark.'

sentences.zh: 譬如養鷹，饑則爲用，飽則揚去。

translations.literal: 'It is like raising a hawk—when hungry it is useful; when full it flies away.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Raising you is like falconry: hunger keeps you loyal; a full crop sends you off.'

sentences.zh: 』其言如此。

translations.literal: His words were like this.
translations.idiomatic: That was how he put it.'

sentences.zh: 」布意乃解。

translations.literal: Bu's mood thereupon eased.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's anger cooled.

sentences.zh: 術怒，與韓暹、楊奉等連勢，遣大將張勳攻布。

translations.literal: Shu was angry; joining forces with Han Xian, Yang Feng, and others, he sent grand general Zhang Xun to attack Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yuan Shu allied with Han Xian and Yang Feng and dispatched Zhang Xun against Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 布謂珪曰：「今致術軍，卿之由也，爲之柰何？

translations.literal: Bu said to Gui: 'Now it has brought Shu's army—it is by your doing; what is to be done about it?'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu asked Chen Gui, 'This army from Yuan Shu—your doing. What now?'

sentences.zh: 」珪曰：「暹、奉與術，卒合之軍耳，策謀不素定，不能相維持，子登策之，比之連雞，勢不俱棲，可解離也。

translations.literal: Gui said: 'Xian and Feng with Shu are a hastily united army only; their strategies were not planned beforehand—they cannot sustain each other. Your son Deng appraises them: compared to chickens tied in a line, their situation cannot perch together—they can be separated.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui answered, 'Han Xian and Yang Feng form only a marriage of convenience with Yuan Shu; no plan binds them. My son Deng compares them to chickens tied together—they cannot roost on one perch—and they can be split apart.'

sentences.zh: 」布用珪策，遣人說暹、奉，使與己并力共擊術軍，軍資所有，悉許暹、奉。

translations.literal: Bu employed Gui's strategy, sent men to persuade Xian and Feng, causing them to join strength with himself and together strike Shu's army; all army supplies and goods were promised to Xian and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu followed this advice, sent envoys to Han Xian and Yang Feng, and promised them all captured materiel if they would join him against Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 於是暹、奉從之，勳大破敗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xian and Feng followed him; Xun was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed, and Zhang Xun's army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》載布與暹、奉書曰：「二將軍拔大駕來東，有元功於國，當書勳竹帛，萬世不朽。

translations.literal: The Jiuzhou Chunqiu records Bu's letter to Xian and Feng, saying: 'The two generals extricated the Great Carriage and came east—they have prime merit toward the state; their deeds ought to be written on bamboo and silk, imperishable for myriad ages.'
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of the Nine Provinces preserves Lü Bu's letter: 'You rescued the emperor and brought him east—merit fit for the histories and an undying name.'

sentences.zh: 今袁術造逆，當共誅討，奈何與賊臣還共伐布？

translations.literal: 'Now Yuan Shu creates rebellion—ought we not join to punish him? How can you together with a traitorous minister return to jointly attack Bu?'
translations.idiomatic: 'Yuan Shu rebels—why march with a traitor against me instead of punishing him?'

sentences.zh: 布有殺董卓之功，與二將軍俱爲功臣，可因今共擊破術，建功於天下，此時不可失也。

translations.literal: 'Bu has the merit of killing Dong Zhuo; together with the two generals he is a meritorious minister—you may take this occasion jointly to strike and destroy Shu and establish merit in the realm—this moment cannot be lost.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I slew Dong Zhuo, as did you in your way—strike Yuan Shu now and win glory while you can.'

sentences.zh: 」暹、奉得書，即迴計從布。

translations.literal: When Xian and Feng received the letter, they immediately turned their plan and followed Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian and Yang Feng switched sides as soon as they read it.

sentences.zh: 布進軍，去勳等營百步，暹、奉兵同時並發，斬十將首，殺傷墮水死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Bu advanced his army, one hundred paces from Xun and others' camp; Xian's and Feng's troops simultaneously all burst forth, beheaded ten generals' heads, and those killed, wounded, or drowned could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu drew up within a hundred paces of Zhang Xun's camp; Han Xian and Yang Feng struck together, took ten generals' heads, and left casualties beyond count in the water.

sentences.zh: 《英雄記》曰：布後又與暹、奉二軍向壽春，水陸並進，所過虜略。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Later Bu again together with Xian's and Feng's two armies headed toward Shouchun, advancing by water and land together, and wherever they passed they seized and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes adds that Lü Bu later marched on Shouchun with Han Xian and Yang Feng by land and river, pillaging as they went.

sentences.zh: 到鍾離，大獲而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhongli, they greatly captured booty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Zhongli, looted heavily, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 旣渡淮北，留書與術曰：「足下恃軍彊盛，常言猛將武士，欲相吞滅，每抑止之耳！

translations.literal: Having crossed north of the Huai, he left a letter for Shu, saying: 'You rely on your army's strength and abundance, constantly speak of fierce generals and warrior knights, and wish mutually to swallow and destroy—I only restrain and stop it!'
translations.idiomatic: North of the Huai he left Yuan Shu a letter: 'You boast of your hosts and brag of swallowing every rival—I have held you back until now!'

sentences.zh: 布雖無勇，虎步淮南，一時之間，足下鼠竄壽春，無出頭者。

translations.literal: 'Bu though without courage, tiger-strides across Huainan; in a single interval you scurry like a rat at Shouchun—there is none who sticks out his head.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I may lack valor, yet I strode across Huainan like a tiger while you cowered in Shouchun like a rat afraid to show your face.'

sentences.zh: 猛將武士，爲悉何在？

translations.literal: 'The fierce generals and warrior knights—where are they all?'
translations.idiomatic: 'Where are those famous warriors now?'

sentences.zh: 足下喜爲大言以誣天下，天下之人安可盡誣？

translations.literal: 'You delight in making grand words to deceive the realm—how can the people of the realm all be deceived?'
translations.idiomatic: 'You love bombast—do you think you can fool everyone under heaven?'

sentences.zh: 古者兵交，使在其間，造策者非布先唱也。

translations.literal: 'In antiquity when armies crossed, envoys went between; the one who first devised the policy was not Bu singing first.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Ancient armies exchanged envoys—I did not provoke this war.'

sentences.zh: 相去不遠，可復相聞。

translations.literal: 'We are separated by no great distance—we can again hear from each other.'
translations.idiomatic: 'We are close enough—send word when you wish.'

sentences.zh: 」布渡畢，術自將步騎五千揚兵淮上，布騎皆於水北大咍笑之而還。

translations.literal: When Bu finished crossing, Shu personally led five thousand foot and cavalry and displayed troops on the Huai; Bu's cavalry all on the north of the water loudly laughed at him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Bu crossed, Yuan Shu led five thousand men to brandish arms along the Huai; Lü Bu's horsemen on the north bank jeered and rode away.

sentences.zh: 時有東海蕭建爲琅邪相，治莒，保城自守，不與布通。

translations.literal: At that time there was Xiao Jian of Donghai, who was chancellor of Langya, ruling from Ju, securing the city and self-defending, and not communicating with Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jian of Donghai was governing Langya from Ju, holding his walls and refusing all contact with Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 布與建書曰：「天下舉兵，本以誅董卓爾。

translations.literal: Bu wrote a letter to Jian, saying: 'The realm raised arms, originally in order to execute Dong Zhuo only.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu wrote: 'The coalition rose only to destroy Dong Zhuo.'

sentences.zh: 布殺卓，來詣關東，欲求兵西迎大駕，光復洛京，諸將自還相攻，莫肯念國。

translations.literal: Bu killed Zhuo, came to east of the pass, wished to seek troops to go west and welcome the Great Carriage, and restore the Luo capital; the generals on their own returned and attacked one another, none willing to think of the state.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I killed Dong Zhuo, reached the east, and begged for men to escort the emperor west and recover Luoyang, but the lords only turned on one another and forgot the throne.'

sentences.zh: 布，五原人也，去徐州五千餘里，乃在天西北角，今不來共爭天東南之地。

translations.literal: 'Bu is a man of Wuyuan, more than five thousand li from Xu Province—he is in the northwest corner of heaven; now I do not come to contest with you the land in the southeast corner of heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I was born in Wuyuan, five thousand li from here in the far northwest; I have not come to fight you for the southeast.'

sentences.zh: 莒與下邳相去不遠，宜當共通。

translations.literal: Ju and Xiapi are separated by no great distance; you ought to communicate in common.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Ju lies near Xiapi—we should be allies.'

sentences.zh: 君如自遂以爲郡郡作帝，縣縣自王也！

translations.literal: 'If you follow your own wish, thinking each commandery makes an emperor, each district makes a king!'
translations.idiomatic: 'Or do you fancy every district an empire and every county a throne?'

sentences.zh: 昔樂毅攻齊，呼吸下齊七十餘城，唯莒、即墨二城不下，所以然者，中有田單故也。

translations.literal: Formerly Yue Yi attacked Qi; in a breath he took more than seventy cities of Qi—only the two cities Ju and Jimo did not fall; the reason was that within there was Tian Dan.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Yue Yi swept Qi in weeks—only Ju and Jimo held out because Tian Dan defended them.'

sentences.zh: 布雖非樂毅，君亦非田單，可取布書與智者詳共議之。

translations.literal: 'Bu though is not Yue Yi, and you also are not Tian Dan—you may take Bu's letter and with wise men deliberate it in detail.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I am no Yue Yi and you are no Tian Dan—show this letter to wise counsel.'

sentences.zh: 」建得書，即遣主簿齎牋上禮，貢良馬五匹。

translations.literal: When Jian received the letter, he immediately sent his chief clerk to bear a note and present gifts, contributing five fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jian answered at once, sending his registrar with a courteous note and five good horses.

sentences.zh: 建尋爲臧霸所襲破，得建資實。

translations.literal: Jian before long was surprised and broken by Zang Ba, who seized Jian's goods and substance.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba soon overran him and seized his stores.

sentences.zh: 布聞之，自將步騎向莒。

translations.literal: When Bu heard it, he personally led foot and cavalry toward Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Lü Bu marched on Ju in person.

sentences.zh: 高順諫曰：「將軍躬殺董卓，威震夷狄，端坐顧盼，遠近自然畏服，不宜輕自出軍；

translations.literal: Gao Shun remonstrated, saying: 'The General personally killed Dong Zhuo; his might shakes the Yi and Di—sitting upright, looking about, far and near naturally fear and submit—it is not appropriate lightly to go out with the army yourself;'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shun urged caution: 'You slew Dong Zhuo and awe the frontier peoples—your very gaze commands fear. Do not rashly take the field.'

sentences.zh: 如或不捷，損名非小。

translations.literal: 'If perhaps it is not victorious, the harm to reputation is not small.'
translations.idiomatic: 'A defeat would cost you more than a battle.'

sentences.zh: 」布不從。

translations.literal: Bu did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu ignored him.

sentences.zh: 霸畏布鈔暴，果登城拒守。

translations.literal: Ba feared Bu's raiding violence; indeed he ascended the city and resisted defense.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Lü Bu's plundering, Zang Ba manned the walls.

sentences.zh: 布不能拔，引還下邳。

translations.literal: Bu could not take it; he led his force back to Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu failed to storm the city and withdrew to Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 霸後復與布和。〉

translations.literal: Ba afterward again made peace with Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba later reconciled with Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 建安三年，布復叛爲術，遣高順攻劉備於沛，破之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jian'an, Bu again rebelled on behalf of Shu, sent Gao Shun to attack Liu Bei at Pei, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 198 Lü Bu renewed his ties to Yuan Shu and sent Gao Shun against Liu Bei at Pei, routing him.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣夏侯惇救備，爲順所敗。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor sent Xiahou Dun to rescue Bei; he was defeated by Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao dispatched Xiahou Dun to Liu Bei's aid, but Gao Shun defeated him.

sentences.zh: 太祖自征布，至其城下，遺布書，爲陳禍福。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor personally campaigned against Bu, arrived below his city walls, and sent Bu a letter laying out fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao led the expedition himself, drew up beneath Xiapi, and wrote Lü Bu with an appeal weighing surrender against ruin.

sentences.zh: 布欲降，陳宮等自以負罪深，沮其計。

translations.literal: Bu wished to surrender; Chen Gong and others, considering themselves deeply guilty of crimes, obstructed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was ready to yield, but Chen Gong and his faction—knowing Cao Cao would never spare them—blocked him.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝春秋》曰：太祖軍至彭城。

translations.literal: The Xiandi Chunqiu says: Grand Progenitor's army reached Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Xian record Cao Cao's army reaching Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 陳宮謂布：「宜逆擊之，以逸擊勞，無不克也。

translations.literal: Chen Gong said to Bu: 'You ought to strike them coming—use rest to strike weariness—there is none you cannot overcome.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong urged a spoiling attack: 'Hit them while they march—fresh troops against weary ones—and you cannot lose.'

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「不如待其來攻，蹙著泗水中。

translations.literal: Bu said: 'It is better to await their coming attack and squeeze them into the Si River water.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu preferred to wait and drive them into the Si River.'

sentences.zh: 」及太祖軍攻之急，布於白門樓上謂軍士曰：「卿曹無相困，我當自首明公。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor's army attacked urgently, Bu on the White Gate Tower said to the soldiers: 'You crowd must not distress one another—I ought myself to surrender to the enlightened lord.'
translations.idiomatic: When the siege tightened, Lü Bu mounted the White Gate Tower and told his men to spare him further shame—he would surrender to Lord Cao himself.'

sentences.zh: 」陳宮曰：「逆賊曹操，何等明公！

translations.literal: Chen Gong said: 'The traitorous thief Cao Cao—what sort of enlightened lord!'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong shouted back, 'That traitor Cao Cao—what enlightened lord is he?'

sentences.zh: 今日降之，若卵投石，豈可得全也！」〉

translations.literal: 'Today if you surrender to him, it is like eggs cast against stone—how can you obtain preservation!'
translations.idiomatic: 'Surrender now and you might as well smash eggs on rock!'

sentences.zh: 布遣人求救於術，自將千餘騎出戰，敗走，還保城，不敢出。

translations.literal: Bu sent men to beg rescue from Shu; personally leading over a thousand riders he went out to battle, was defeated and fled, returned to protect the city, and did not dare go out.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu begged Yuan Shu for help, led a thousand riders in a sortie, was beaten back, and shut himself inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：布遣許汜、王楷告急於術。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Bu sent Xu Si and Wang Kai to report urgency to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes names Xu Si and Wang Kai as his envoys to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術曰：「布不與我女，理自當敗，何爲復來相聞邪？

translations.literal: Shu said: 'Bu did not give me his daughter—by principle he ought himself to be defeated—why again come to inform me?'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu replied, 'He broke our marriage pact—defeat is his own fault—why bother me again?'

sentences.zh: 」汜、楷曰：「明上今不救布，爲自敗耳！

translations.literal: Si and Kai said: 'If the enlightened sovereign above now does not rescue Bu, it is for himself to be defeated!'
translations.idiomatic: They warned him, 'Refuse Lü Bu now and you doom yourself.'

sentences.zh: 布破，明上亦破也。

translations.literal: 'If Bu is broken, the enlightened sovereign above is also broken.'
translations.idiomatic: 'If he falls, you fall with him.'

sentences.zh: 」術時僭號，故呼爲明上。

translations.literal: At that time Shu had usurped the title; therefore he was called enlightened sovereign above.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu had proclaimed himself emperor, hence the deferential 'Your Enlightened Majesty.'

sentences.zh: 術乃嚴兵爲布作聲援。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon marshaled troops to make a sounding aid for Bu.
translations.idiomatic: He massed troops as a gesture of support.

sentences.zh: 布恐術爲女不至，故不遣兵救也，以緜纏女身，縛著馬上，夜自送女出與術，與太祖守兵相觸，格射不得過，復還城。

translations.literal: Bu feared that Shu, because the daughter had not arrived, therefore did not send troops to rescue; he wrapped the daughter's body in silk floss, bound her on a horse, and by night personally escorted the daughter out to Shu; they clashed with Grand Progenitor's guarding troops, were blocked by crossbow fire and could not pass, and returned to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu suspected Yuan Shu withheld aid until the bride appeared, so he swathed his daughter in silk, lashed her to a saddle, and tried to ride her through Cao Cao's lines by night; volleys drove him back.

sentences.zh: 布欲令陳宮、高順守城，自將騎斷太祖糧道。

translations.literal: Bu wished to have Chen Gong and Gao Shun defend the city; personally leading cavalry he would cut Grand Progenitor's grain road.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to leave Chen Gong and Gao Shun to hold Xiapi while he raided Cao Cao's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 布妻謂曰：「將軍自出斷曹公糧道是也。

translations.literal: Bu's wife said to him: 'For the General personally to go out and cut Lord Cao's grain road is right.'
translations.idiomatic: His wife agreed that cutting Cao Cao's supplies made sense.

sentences.zh: 宮、順素不和，將軍一出，宮、順必不同心共城守也，如有蹉跌，將軍當於何自立乎？

translations.literal: 'Gong and Shun by nature are not harmonious; once the General goes out, Gong and Shun will surely not be of one heart in jointly defending the city—if there is a slip, where will the General establish himself?'
translations.idiomatic: 'But Gong and Shun hardly cooperate—leave them alone and the city may fall; then where will you stand?'

sentences.zh: 願將軍諦計之，無爲宮等所誤也。

translations.literal: 'I wish the General would deliberate carefully on it—do not be misled by Gong and the others.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Think hard—do not let Chen Gong gamble away your life.'

sentences.zh: 妾昔在長安，已爲將軍所棄，賴得龐舒私藏妾身耳，今不須顧妾也。

translations.literal: 'Your concubine formerly at Chang'an was already abandoned by the General; I depended on obtaining Pang Shu privately hiding your concubine's body—now you need not consider your concubine.'
translations.idiomatic: 'You abandoned me once in Chang'an—I survived only because Pang Shu hid me. Forget about me now.'

sentences.zh: 」布得妻言，愁悶不能自決。

translations.literal: When Bu obtained his wife's words, he was anxious and gloomy and could not decide himself.
translations.idiomatic: Her words left him paralyzed with doubt.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：陳宮謂布曰：「曹公遠來，勢不能久。

translations.literal: The Wei shi Chunqiu says: Chen Gong said to Bu: 'Lord Cao has come from afar—his situation cannot endure long.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Chronicle quotes Chen Gong: 'Cao Cao marched far—he cannot keep this up.'

sentences.zh: 若將軍以步騎出屯，爲勢於外，宮將餘衆閉守於內，若向將軍，宮引兵而攻其背，若來攻城，將軍爲救於外。

translations.literal: 'If the General with foot and cavalry goes out and encamps, making a posture outside, Gong will lead the remaining masses to shut and defend within—if they turn toward the General, Gong will lead troops and attack their rear; if they come to attack the city, the General will rescue from outside.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Camp outside with the bulk of your horse and foot while I hold the walls—if they chase you, I strike their rear; if they besiege me, you relieve them from outside.'

sentences.zh: 不過旬日，軍食必盡，擊之可破。

translations.literal: 'Within no more than ten days their army provisions must be exhausted—strike them and they can be broken.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Their provisions will fail within ten days—then we crush them.'

sentences.zh: 」布然之。

translations.literal: Bu approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu agreed.

sentences.zh: 布妻曰：「昔曹氏待公臺如赤子，猶舍而來。

translations.literal: Bu's wife said: 'Formerly the Cao clan treated Gongtai like a newborn infant—yet he left and came.'
translations.idiomatic: His wife objected: 'Cao Cao once cherished Chen Gong like a child—yet Gong deserted him for you.'

sentences.zh: 今將軍厚公臺不過於曹公，而欲委全城，捐妻子，孤軍遠出，若一旦有變，妾豈得爲將軍妻哉！

translations.literal: 'Now the General treats Gongtai generously no more than Lord Cao, yet wishes to entrust the whole city, cast aside wife and children, and with an isolated army go far out—if once there is a change, how can your concubine obtain to be the General's wife!'
translations.idiomatic: 'You barely trust Chen Gong more than Cao Cao did—yet you would stake the city, your family, and a lone sortie on him. If anything goes wrong, I am no longer your wife!'

sentences.zh: 」布乃止。〉

translations.literal: Bu thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 術亦不能救。

translations.literal: Shu also could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu could not save him either.

sentences.zh: 布雖驍猛，然無謀而多猜忌，不能制御其黨，但信諸將。

translations.literal: Bu though fierce and bold, yet was without strategy and much suspicious, could not control and restrain his clique, only trusted the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce as Lü Bu was, he lacked judgment, suspected everyone, failed to master his own faction, and put blind faith in his officers.

sentences.zh: 諸將各異意自疑，故每戰多敗。

translations.literal: The various generals each had different ideas and self-doubt; therefore in each battle they were often defeated.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders doubted one another and rarely won a fight.

sentences.zh: 太祖塹圍之三月，上下離心，其將侯成、宋憲、魏續縛陳宮，將其衆降。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor trenched and besieged them three months; high and low lost heart from one another; his generals Hou Cheng, Song Xian, and Wei Xu bound Chen Gong and led their masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After three months of trench warfare the garrison came apart: Hou Cheng, Song Xian, and Wei Xu seized Chen Gong and surrendered with their men.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：初，布騎將侯成遣客牧馬十五匹，客悉驅馬去，向沛城，欲歸劉備。

translations.literal: The Jiuzhou Chunqiu says: At first Bu's cavalry general Hou Cheng sent a client to herd fifteen horses; the client drove all the horses away toward Pei city, wishing to return to Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of the Nine Provinces explains that Hou Cheng had entrusted fifteen horses to a groom who bolted toward Pei to rejoin Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 成自將騎逐之，悉得馬還。

translations.literal: Cheng himself led cavalry to pursue them and entirely got the horses back.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Cheng rode after him and recovered every horse.

sentences.zh: 諸將合禮賀成，成釀五六斛酒，獵得十餘頭豬，未飲食，先持半豬五斗酒自入詣布前，跪言：「間蒙將軍恩，逐得所失馬，諸將來相賀，自釀少酒，獵得豬，未敢飲食，先奉上微意。

translations.literal: The generals jointly with ritual congratulated Cheng; Cheng brewed five or six hu of wine, hunted and obtained more than ten pigs; before drinking or eating, he first took half a pig and five dou of wine, himself entered and went before Bu, knelt and said: 'Recently I have received the General's grace and pursued and recovered the lost horses; the generals come to congratulate one another; I brewed a little wine and hunted and obtained pigs; I did not dare drink or eat—I first offer my slight intent.'
translations.idiomatic: The officers congratulated him with ceremony. Hou Cheng brewed several hu of wine, bagged a dozen pigs, and carried half a pig and five dou of wine to Lü Bu before touching his own feast. Kneeling, he said: 'Your Grace helped me recover my horses; my comrades wished to celebrate, so I brewed a little wine and took game—but I would not taste it until I offered the first share to you.'

sentences.zh: 」布大怒曰：「布禁酒，卿釀酒，諸將共飲食作兄弟，共謀殺布邪？

translations.literal: Bu greatly angry said: 'Bu forbids wine; you brew wine; the generals together drink and eat and act as brothers—are you jointly plotting to kill Bu?'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu thundered: 'I banned liquor—you brewed it, you feasted like sworn brothers—do you mean to murder me?'

sentences.zh: 」成大懼而去，棄所釀酒，還諸將禮。

translations.literal: Cheng greatly feared and departed, cast away the wine he had brewed, and returned the generals' gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Hou Cheng poured out the wine and gave back the congratulatory gifts.

sentences.zh: 由是自疑，會太祖圍下邳，成遂領衆降。〉

translations.literal: From this he self-suspected; when it happened that Grand Progenitor besieged Xiapi, Cheng thereupon led the masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He began to fear for his life; when Cao Cao invested Xiapi, he opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 布與其麾下登白門樓。

translations.literal: Bu together with his subordinates ascended the White Gate Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu and his retinue climbed the White Gate Tower.

sentences.zh: 兵圍急，乃下降。

translations.literal: The army besieged urgently, and he thereupon came down in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: With the noose tightening, he came down to surrender.

sentences.zh: 遂生縛布，布曰：「縛太急，小緩之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they bound Bu alive; Bu said: 'The binding is too tight—loosen it a little.'
translations.idiomatic: They took him alive. 'The ropes are too tight,' Lü Bu said, 'give me a little slack.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「縛虎不得不急也。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: 'Binding a tiger cannot but be tight.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered, 'This is how you tie a tiger.'

sentences.zh: 」布請曰：「明公所患不過於布，今已服矣，天下不足憂。

translations.literal: Bu begged, saying: 'What the enlightened lord troubles over is no more than Bu; now I have submitted—the realm is not worth worrying about.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu pleaded: 'I am the only thorn in your side, and I yield—think what that means for the rest of the realm.'

sentences.zh: 明公將步，令布將騎，則天下不足定也。

translations.literal: Let the enlightened lord command the foot soldiers and Bu command the cavalry—then the realm is not worth settling.'
translations.idiomatic: Put me at the head of your horse—and you will pacify the empire.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖有疑色。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor had a doubting expression.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao hesitated.

sentences.zh: 劉備進曰：「明公不見布之事丁建陽及董太師乎！

translations.literal: Liu Bei advanced and said: 'Does not the enlightened lord remember Bu's dealings with Ding Jianyang and Grand Tutor Dong!'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei put in: 'My lord, remember Ding Yuan—and Dong Zhuo.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖頷之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor nodded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao nodded.

sentences.zh: 布因指備曰：「是兒最叵信者。」

translations.literal: Bu therefore pointed at Bei and said: 'This boy is the least trustworthy.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu jabbed a finger at Liu Bei. 'That man is the worst oath-breaker alive.'

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：布謂太祖曰：「布待諸將厚也，諸將臨急皆叛布耳。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Bu said to Grand Progenitor: 'Bu treats the generals generously; when urgent the generals all betray Bu.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes quotes Lü Bu: 'I treated my officers well—they deserted me in crisis.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「卿背妻，愛諸將婦，何以爲厚？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: 'You betray your wives yet love the generals' wives—how is that generous?'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao shot back: 'You betray your wife for other men's wives—some generosity.'

sentences.zh: 」布默然。

translations.literal: Bu was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu had no reply.

sentences.zh: 《獻帝春秋》曰：布問太祖：「明公何瘦？

translations.literal: The Xiandi Chunqiu says: Bu asked Grand Progenitor: 'Why is the enlightened lord thin?'
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Xian record Lü Bu asking why Cao Cao looked gaunt.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「君何以識孤？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: 'How do you recognize me in solitude?'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked how they had met.

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「昔在洛，會溫氏園。

translations.literal: Bu said: 'Formerly at Luoyang we met at the Wen clan garden.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu said they had crossed paths in Luoyang at the Wen family's estate.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「然。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: 'So it is.'
translations.idiomatic: 'So we did,' said Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 孤忘之矣。

translations.literal: I forgot it.
translations.idiomatic: He had forgotten.

sentences.zh: 所以瘦，恨不早相得故也。

translations.literal: The reason I am thin is that I regret not having obtained each other earlier.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed his wasted frame on having discovered Lü Bu too late.

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「齊桓舍射鉤，使管仲相；

translations.literal: Bu said: 'Duke Huan of Qi forgave the arrow in his belt-hook and made Guan Zhong his minister;'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu cited Duke Huan, who forgave Guan Zhong's arrow.

sentences.zh: 今使布竭股肱之力，爲公前驅，可乎？

translations.literal: Now let Bu exhaust the strength of thighs and arms and be your vanguard—may it be done?'
translations.idiomatic: Let me bend every muscle as your vanguard—will you have me?'

sentences.zh: 」布縛急，謂劉備曰：「玄德，卿爲坐客，我爲執虜，不能一言以相寬乎？

translations.literal: Bu was bound tight and said to Liu Bei: 'Xuande, you are seated guest and I am bound captive—can you not speak one word to widen mercy for me?'
translations.idiomatic: Bound tight, he cried to Liu Bei: 'You sit free while I am trussed—will you not speak for me?'

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑曰：「何不相語，而訴明使君乎？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor laughed and said: 'Why did you not speak to each other, yet complain to the enlightened shepherd?'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed: 'Why plead with Xuande instead of asking me yourself?'

sentences.zh: 」意欲活之，命使寬縛。

translations.literal: His intent wished to spare him; he ordered his bonds loosened.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to spare Lü Bu and ordered the ropes slackened.

sentences.zh: 主簿王必趨進曰：「布，勍虜也。

translations.literal: Registrar Wang Bi hurried forward and said: 'Bu is a fierce captive.'
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Wang Bi protested: 'Lü Bu is too dangerous to spare.'

sentences.zh: 其衆近在外，不可寬也。

translations.literal: His masses are near outside—they cannot be treated leniently.'
translations.idiomatic: His troops still surround us—we cannot risk it.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「本欲相緩，主簿復不聽，如之何？」〉

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: 'Originally I wished to ease them for you, but the registrar again will not listen—what is to be done?'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said with a shrug, 'I would loosen them, but my registrar forbids it—what can I do?'

sentences.zh: 於是縊殺布。

translations.literal: Thereupon they strangled Bu to death.
translations.idiomatic: They strangled Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 布與宮、順等皆梟首送許，然後葬之。

translations.literal: Bu together with Gong, Shun, and others all had their heads displayed and sent to Xu; afterward they were buried.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu, Chen Gong, Gao Shun, and the rest were beheaded; their heads went to Xu before the bodies were buried.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：順爲人清白有威嚴，不飲酒，不受饋遺。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Shun as a man was pure and white, possessed awe-inspiring dignity, did not drink wine, and did not accept gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes describes Gao Shun as austere, formidable, abstemious, and incorruptible.

sentences.zh: 所將七百餘兵，號爲千人，鎧甲鬬具皆精練齊整，每所攻擊無不破者，名爲陷陣營。

translations.literal: The more than seven hundred soldiers he led were titled a thousand; armor and combat gear were all refined and trim; wherever they attacked none did not break—they were named the Formation-breakers Camp.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded some seven hundred men who passed as a thousand, in flawless armor—every assault succeeded—known as the Camp That Breaks the Line.

sentences.zh: 順每諫布，言「凡破家亡國，非無忠臣明智者也，但患不見用耳。

translations.literal: Shun often remonstrated with Bu, saying 'Whenever families are ruined and states lost, it is not that there are no loyal ministers and wise men—only the worry is they are not employed.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shun often warned Lü Bu: 'States fall not for lack of loyal men but because rulers refuse counsel.'

sentences.zh: 將軍舉動，不肯詳思，輙喜言誤，誤不可數也」。

translations.literal: The General's actions are unwilling to deliberate carefully; readily he delights in mistaken words—mistakes cannot be counted.'
translations.idiomatic: 'You rush every decision and pile mistake on mistake.'

sentences.zh: 布知其忠，然不能用。

translations.literal: Bu knew his loyalty, yet could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu knew he was honest yet never followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 布從郝萌反後，更疏順。

translations.literal: After Bu followed Hao Meng's rebellion, he became more distant from Shun.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao Meng's mutiny Lü Bu grew colder toward Gao Shun.

sentences.zh: 以魏續有外內之親，悉奪順所將兵以與續。

translations.literal: Because Wei Xu had inner and outer kinship, he entirely stripped the troops Shun led and gave them to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Gao Shun's command and gave the troops to his wife's relative Wei Xu.

sentences.zh: 及當攻戰，故令順將續所領兵，順亦終無恨意。〉

translations.literal: When it came time to attack in battle, he therefore ordered Shun to command the troops Xu led; Shun to the end had no resentful intent.
translations.idiomatic: When battle came he made Gao Shun lead Wei Xu's men; Gao Shun showed no resentment.

sentences.zh: 太祖之禽宮也，問宮欲活老母及女不？

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor captured Gong, he asked Gong whether he wished to spare his old mother and daughter or not?
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Gong's capture Cao Cao asked whether he wanted his mother and daughter spared.

sentences.zh: 宮對曰：「宮聞孝治天下者不絕人之親，仁施四海者不乏人之祀，老母在公，不在宮也。

translations.literal: Gong replied: 'Gong has heard that one who governs the realm with filial piety does not cut off others' kin; one who extends benevolence within the four seas does not exhaust others' sacrifices—the old mother is with you, not with Gong.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong answered that a ruler who truly honors filial piety and benevolence leaves families intact—his mother's fate rested with Cao Cao, not with him.

sentences.zh: 」太祖召養其母終其身，嫁其女。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor summoned and supported his mother for her whole life and married off his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao supported Chen Gong's mother for life and saw his daughter married.

sentences.zh: 〈魚氏《典略》曰：陳宮字公臺，東郡人也。

translations.literal: The Yu clan Dian lüe says: Chen Gong, style name Gongtai, was a man of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan's Comprehensive Survey gives Chen Gong's courtesy name as Gongtai and his origin in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 剛直烈壯，少與海內知名之士皆相連結。

translations.literal: He was upright, fierce, and stalwart; in youth he connected with all renowned gentlemen within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and bold, he befriamed every famous scholar of the age.

sentences.zh: 及天下亂，始隨太祖，後自疑，乃從呂布，爲布畫策，布每不從其計。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into chaos, at first he followed Grand Progenitor; afterward he self-suspected, then followed Lü Bu, planning strategy for Bu; Bu often did not follow his plans.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos came he first served Cao Cao, then doubted him and joined Lü Bu—whose plans he drew and routinely ignored.

sentences.zh: 下邳敗，軍士執布及宮，太祖皆見之，與語平生，故布有求活之言。

translations.literal: When Xiapi fell, soldiers seized Bu and Gong; Grand Progenitor saw them both, spoke with them of their whole lives—therefore Bu had words seeking to live.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiapi's fall Lü Bu and Chen Gong were brought before Cao Cao, who spoke of old times—hence Lü Bu's plea for life.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂宮曰：「公臺，卿平常自謂智計有餘，今竟何如？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said to Gong: 'Gongtai, you ordinarily called your stratagems more than sufficient—now in the end how is it?'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked, 'Gongtai, you always claimed superior wit—how did it end?'

sentences.zh: 」宮顧指布曰：「但坐此人不從宮言，以至於此。

translations.literal: Gong turned and pointed at Bu, saying: 'Only because this man did not follow Gong's words did it reach this.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong pointed at Lü Bu: 'Because he never listened to me.'

sentences.zh: 若其見從，亦未必爲禽也。

translations.literal: If he had followed me, one also would not necessarily have been captured.'
translations.idiomatic: Had he listened, we might not stand here.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑曰：「今日之事當云何？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor laughed and said: 'Today's affair—how ought it to be?'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked what should happen now.

sentences.zh: 」宮曰：「爲臣不忠，爲子不孝，死自分也。

translations.literal: Gong said: 'As a minister not loyal, as a son not filial—death is my proper portion.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong said he deserved death for disloyalty and unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「卿如是，柰卿老母何？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: 'If you are thus, what of your old mother?'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked after his mother.

sentences.zh: 」宮曰：「宮聞將以孝治天下者不害人之親，老母之存否，在明公也。

translations.literal: Gong said: 'Gong has heard that one who will rule with filial piety does not harm others' kin—whether the old mother lives or dies is with the enlightened lord.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong replied that a sovereign who rules by filial piety does not punish families—her life was Cao Cao's to decide.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「若卿妻子何？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: 'What of your wife and children?'
translations.idiomatic: And your wife and children?

sentences.zh: 」宮曰：「宮聞將施仁政於天下者不絕人之祀，妻子之存否，亦在明公也。

translations.literal: Gong said: 'Gong has heard that one who will extend humane government within the four seas does not cut off others' sacrifices—whether wife and children live or die is also with the enlightened lord.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong repeated that a humane ruler preserves heirs—their fate too rested with Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 」太祖未復言。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor did not reply again.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao fell silent.

sentences.zh: 宮曰：「請出就戮，以明軍法。

translations.literal: Gong said: 'I request to go out and accept execution, to clarify military law.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong asked leave to die by the law of war.

sentences.zh: 」遂趨出，不可止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he hastened out and could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He walked out; no one could stop him.

sentences.zh: 太祖泣而送之，宮不還顧。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor wept as he sent him off; Gong did not turn his head back.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wept at the gate; Chen Gong never looked back.

sentences.zh: 宮死後，太祖待其家皆厚於初。〉

translations.literal: After Gong died, Grand Progenitor treated his family all more generously than at first.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Cao Cao treated Chen Gong's kin even better than before.

sentences.zh: 陳登者，字元龍，在廣陵有威名。

translations.literal: As for Chen Deng, style name Yuanlong, at Guangling he had awe-inspiring reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng, courtesy name Yuanlong, enjoyed wide renown in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 又掎角呂布有功，加伏波將軍，年三十九卒。

translations.literal: Also he pincered Lü Bu with effective merit, was advanced General Who Calms the Waves, and died at age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: His role in crushing Lü Bu earned him the title General Who Calms the Waves; he died at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 後許汜與劉備並在荊州牧劉表坐，表與備共論天下人，汜曰：「陳元龍湖海之士，豪氣不除。

translations.literal: Later Xu Si together with Liu Bei both sat in Governor of Jingzhou Liu Biao's presence; Biao together with Bei discussed people of the realm; Si said: 'Chen Yuanlong is a lakes-and-seas knight—his heroic spirit is not removed.'
translations.idiomatic: Later Xu Si sat with Liu Bei at Liu Biao's table; when talk turned to worthies Xu Si called Chen Deng a brash wanderer who never shed his swagger.

sentences.zh: 」備謂表曰：「許君論是非？

translations.literal: Bei said to Biao: 'Does Sir Xu weigh right and wrong?'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei asked Liu Biao whether Xu Si knew how to judge men.

sentences.zh: 」表曰：「欲言非，此君爲善士，不宜虛言；

translations.literal: Biao said: 'If I wish to say it is not so, this gentleman is a good man—I ought not speak emptily;'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao hedged: calling Xu wrong would insult a good man.

sentences.zh: 欲言是，元龍名重天下。

translations.literal: If I wish to say it is so, Yuanlong's name weighs heavy in the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Calling him right would slight Chen Deng's fame.

sentences.zh: 」備問汜：「君言豪，寧有事邪？

translations.literal: Bei asked Si: 'You speak of heroism—was there indeed an affair?'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei pressed Xu Si for the story.

sentences.zh: 」汜曰：「昔遭亂過下邳，見元龍。

translations.literal: Si said: 'Formerly suffering chaos I passed through Xiapi and saw Yuanlong.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Si said he had visited Chen Deng in Xiapi during the troubles.

sentences.zh: 元龍無客主之意，久不相與語，自上大牀卧，使客卧下牀。

translations.literal: Yuanlong had no intent of host and guest; long he did not converse with me; himself he ascended the great couch to lie; he made the guest lie on the lower couch.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng acted nothing like a host—ignored him, stretched out on the main couch, and relegated Xu Si to the foot bench.
