sentences.zh: 」備曰：「君有國士之名，今天下大亂，帝主失所，望君憂國忘家，有救世之意，而君求田問舍，言無可采，是元龍所諱也，何緣當與君語？

translations.literal: Bei said: 'You have the name of a state knight; today the realm is greatly chaotic, the emperor-host has lost his place—I hoped you would worry for the state and forget home, having intent to save the age; yet you seek fields and ask after houses—your words have nothing worth adopting—this is what Yuanlong avoids; what cause would there be for him to converse with you?'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei rebuked him: in such times a man of stature should worry about the throne, not mortgages—Chen Deng had brushed him off because Xu deserved nothing better.

sentences.zh: 如小人，欲卧百尺樓上，卧君於地，何但上下牀之閒邪？

translations.literal: If it were I, the petty man, I would wish to lie on a hundred-foot tower and lie you on the ground—how only between upper and lower couch!'
translations.idiomatic: Were it Liu Bei, he would seat Xu Si on the floor beneath a hundred-foot loft—not merely the wrong couch.

sentences.zh: 」表大笑。

translations.literal: Biao greatly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 備因言曰：「若元龍文武膽志，當求之於古耳，造次難得比也。」

translations.literal: Bei therefore said: 'If Yuanlong's civil and military courage and resolve—one ought to seek them in antiquity; in haste it is hard to obtain comparison.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei added that Chen Deng's caliber belonged beside the ancients—no modern rival.

sentences.zh: 〈《先賢行狀》曰：登忠亮高爽，沈深有大略，少有扶世濟民之志。

translations.literal: The Xianxian xingzhuang says: Deng was loyal and bright, high-minded and frank, deep and possessed of great strategy; in youth he had the intent to support the age and aid the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Accounts of Worthies describes Chen Deng as loyal, brilliant, far-sighted, and ambitious to save the people.

sentences.zh: 博覽載籍，雅有文藝，舊典文章，莫不貫綜。

translations.literal: He broadly perused carried texts; elegantly he had literary arts; old canons and writings—none he did not thread together.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and mastered classical letters and state papers.

sentences.zh: 年二十五，舉孝廉，除東陽長，養耆育孤，視民如傷。

translations.literal: At age twenty-five he was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, appointed chief of Dongyang, nurtured the aged and raised orphans, looked on the people as wounded.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-five he earned the Filial and Incorrupt nomination and governed Dongyang, caring for elders and orphans as if each citizen were wounded flesh.

sentences.zh: 是時世荒民饑，州牧陶謙表登爲典農校尉，乃巡土田之宜，盡鑿溉之利，秔稻豐積。

translations.literal: At this time the age was waste and the people hungry; Governor Tao Qian memorialized Deng as Colonel Director of Agriculture; he then surveyed the suitability of soil and fields, exhausted the benefit of irrigation and ditches, and glutinous and non-glutinous rice piled abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: In famine times Tao Qian named him agricultural intendant; he surveyed fields, dug irrigation, and filled the granaries with rice.

sentences.zh: 奉使到許，太祖以登爲廣陵太守，令陰合衆以圖呂布。

translations.literal: Sent on mission to Xu, Grand Progenitor appointed Deng Administrator of Guangling, ordering him secretly to unite the masses to plot against Lü Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Called to Xu, Cao Cao made him administrator of Guangling to plot against Lü Bu in secret.

sentences.zh: 登在廣陵，明審賞罰，威信宣布。

translations.literal: Deng at Guangling was clear in investigating rewards and punishments; awe-inspiring trust was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangling his rewards and punishments were transparent and his authority respected.

sentences.zh: 海賊薛州之羣萬有餘戶，束手歸命。

translations.literal: The pirate Xue Zhou's band was more than ten thousand households; they bound hands and submitted to fate.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand pirate households under Xue Zhou surrendered without a fight.

sentences.zh: 未及期年，功化以就，百姓畏而愛之。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed, merit and transformation were accomplished; the hundred surnames feared yet loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year his rule won fear and love.

sentences.zh: 登曰：「此可用矣。

translations.literal: Deng said: 'This can be used.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng said the moment had come.

sentences.zh: 」太祖到下邳，登率郡兵爲軍先驅。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor reached Xiapi, Deng led the command troops as the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao reached Xiapi, Chen Deng led his district troops in the van.

sentences.zh: 時登諸弟在下邳城中，布乃質執登三弟，欲求和同。

translations.literal: At that time Deng's younger brothers were in Xiapi city; Bu then held Deng's three younger brothers hostage, wishing to seek peace and alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu held Chen Deng's three brothers hostage inside Xiapi to force a truce.

sentences.zh: 登執意不撓，進圍日急。

translations.literal: Deng held his intent unyielding; the advance siege daily grew urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng pressed the siege without flinching.

sentences.zh: 布刺姦張弘，懼於後累，夜將登三弟出就登。

translations.literal: Bu's secret-police officer Zhang Hong, fearing later trouble, by night led Deng's three younger brothers out to join Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zhang Hong, fearing reprisals, smuggled the brothers out to Chen Deng by night.

sentences.zh: 布旣伏誅，登以功加拜伏波將軍，甚得江、淮間歡心，於是有吞滅江南之志。

translations.literal: After Bu had been executed by law, Deng by merit was advanced General Who Calms the Waves; he greatly won the hearts of the Jiang and Huai region; thereupon he had intent to swallow and destroy south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Bu's execution Chen Deng earned the title General Who Calms the Waves and the devotion of the Huai River lands—he dreamed of conquering the south.

sentences.zh: 孫策遣軍攻登於匡琦城。

translations.literal: Sun Ce sent troops to attack Deng at Kuangqi city.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce besieged him at Kuangqi.

sentences.zh: 賊初到，旌甲覆水，羣下咸以今賊衆十倍於郡兵，恐不能抗，可引軍避之，與其空城。

translations.literal: When the bandits first arrived, banners and armor covered the water; subordinates all thought that now the bandits were tenfold the command troops and feared they could not resist—they could lead the army away and avoid them, giving them an empty city.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet blotted out the river; his staff urged retreat—Sun Ce outnumbered them ten to one—and counseled yielding an empty city.

sentences.zh: 水人居陸，不能久處，必尋引去。

translations.literal: Water people dwelling on land cannot long remain—they must before long lead away.'
translations.idiomatic: Land-bound sailors cannot stay; they will withdraw.'

sentences.zh: 登厲聲曰：「吾受國命，來鎮此土。

translations.literal: Deng with stern voice said: 'I received the state's command to guard this soil.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng thundered that the court had charged him with this soil.

sentences.zh: 昔馬文淵之在斯位，能南平百越，北滅羣狄，吾旣不能遏除凶慝，何逃寇之謂邪！

translations.literal: Formerly Ma Wenyuan in this position was able south to pacify the hundred Yue and north to destroy the mass Di—since I cannot halt and remove fierce wickedness, what talk of fleeing bandits!'
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan had crushed Yue and Di from this post—how could he flee pirates?'

sentences.zh: 吾其出命以報國，仗義以整亂，天道與順，克之必矣。

translations.literal: I will risk my life to repay the state, take my stand on righteousness to set right disorder; Heaven's way sides with the obedient—victory is certain.'
translations.idiomatic: I will give my life for the Han, ride the cause of justice, and Heaven favors the just—we cannot lose.'

sentences.zh: 」乃閉門自守，示弱不與戰，將士銜聲，寂若無人。

translations.literal: He thereupon closed the gates and held fast, feigned weakness and refused battle; officers and men held their tongues—silent as if the walls were empty.
translations.idiomatic: He shut the gates, played weak, and forbade any sound from the ramparts—dead still.

sentences.zh: 登乘城望形勢，知其可擊，乃申令將士，宿整兵器，昧爽，開南門，引軍指賊營，步騎鈔其後。

translations.literal: Deng mounted the walls to study the terrain, saw his opening, issued strict orders, had weapons readied overnight, and at dawn opened the south gate, drove toward the enemy camp, and hit their rear with foot and horse.
translations.idiomatic: From the battlements Chen Deng saw how to strike: before dawn he ordered weapons prepared, burst from the south gate, and rolled up the enemy rear.

sentences.zh: 賊周章方結陣，不得還舩。

translations.literal: The raiders were still forming ranks and could not regain their boats.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce's men were caught lining up and never made it back to their ships.

sentences.zh: 登手執軍鼓，縱兵乘之，賊遂大破，皆棄舩迸走。

translations.literal: Deng beat the army drum himself, unleashed his troops on the disorder, and shattered them; they abandoned ship and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng sounded the charge himself; the enemy broke, ditched their boats, and ran.

sentences.zh: 登乘勝追奔，斬虜以萬數。

translations.literal: Deng pressed the pursuit and took tens of thousands of heads and prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He chased the rout and counted tens of thousands of enemy killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 賊忿喪軍，尋復大興兵向登。

translations.literal: The enemy, furious at their loss, soon mounted another full-scale attack on Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Smarting from defeat, they returned in strength against Chen Deng.

sentences.zh: 登以兵不敵，使功曹陳矯求救於太祖。

translations.literal: Deng, outmatched in numbers, sent his merit clerk Chen Jiao to beg relief from Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Chen Deng dispatched Chen Jiao to plead with Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 登密去城十里治軍營處所，令多取柴薪，兩束一聚，相去十步，從橫成行，令夜俱起火，火然其聚。

translations.literal: Deng secretly camped ten li from the city, had men stack firewood in pairs ten paces apart in a grid, and ordered every pile lit at night.
translations.idiomatic: He pitched a decamp ten li out, crisscrossed paired bundles of fuel, and set the rows ablaze after dark.

sentences.zh: 城上稱慶，若大軍到。

translations.literal: On the walls his men cheered as though a great host had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison roared welcome as if Cao Cao's main army were there.

sentences.zh: 賊望火驚潰，登勒兵追奔，斬首萬級。

translations.literal: The raiders saw the fires, panicked, and broke; Deng rallied pursuit and took ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The fires routed them; Chen Deng cut off ten thousand heads in the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 遷登爲東城太守。

translations.literal: Deng was promoted Administrator of Dongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The court transferred him to Dongcheng.

sentences.zh: 廣陵吏民佩其恩德，共拔郡隨登，老弱繈負而追之。

translations.literal: The clerks and commoners of Guangling cherished his kindness and tried to uproot the whole commandery to follow him; old and young were carried on backs in the chase.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful Guangling tried to follow him en masse—parents hoisted children on their backs to keep up.

sentences.zh: 登曉語令還，曰：「太守在卿郡，頻致吳寇，幸而克濟。

translations.literal: Deng at dawn urged them home, saying: 'While I governed your district we often drew Wu's raiders—only luck saw us through.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he told them to turn back: 'My tenure invited Wu's attacks—we survived by fortune alone.'

sentences.zh: 諸卿何患無令君乎？

translations.literal: Why fear you will lack another worthy magistrate?'
translations.idiomatic: You will find another good shepherd.'

sentences.zh: 」孫權遂跨有江外。

translations.literal: Sun Quan thereupon spanned the south of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan took everything south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 太祖每臨大江而歎，恨不早用陳元龍計，而令封豕養其爪牙。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor sighed every time he faced the great river, regretting he had not acted sooner on Chen Yuanlong's design and had let the great boar sharpen its tusks.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao never crossed the Yangtze without cursing his delay—Chen Deng could have checked Sun Quan before the beast grew claws.

sentences.zh: 文帝追美登功，拜登息肅爲郎中。〉

translations.literal: Emperor Wen posthumously honored Deng's service and appointed Deng's son Su as Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ennobled Chen Deng's memory and gave his son Su a post at court.

sentences.zh: 臧洪字子源，廣陵射陽人也。

translations.literal: Zang Hong, style name Ziyuan, was a native of Sheyang in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong, courtesy name Ziyuan, came from Sheyang in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 父旻，歷匈奴中郎將、中山、太原太守，所在有名。

translations.literal: His father Min had served successively as Colonel of the Northern Barbarians and as Administrator of Zhongshan and Taiyuan, earning renown wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zang Min served as Han inspector of the northern tribes and as governor of Zhongshan and Taiyuan with a celebrated record.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承《後漢書》曰：旻有幹事才，達於從政，為漢良吏。

translations.literal: Xie Cheng's Later Han says: Min had administrative talent and excelled in government—he was an exemplary Han official.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng records Zang Min as a capable administrator and model officer.

sentences.zh: 初從徐州從事闢司徒府，除盧奴令，冀州舉尤異，遷揚州刺史、丹楊太守。

translations.literal: He began as a clerk in Xu Province, entered the Excellencies' service, became magistrate of Lunu, was nominated outstanding by Ji Province, and rose to Governor of Yangzhou and Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned from Xu clerking to the capital, he governed Lunu, won Ji Province's top nomination, and advanced to Yangzhou governor and Danyang administrator.

sentences.zh: 是時邊方有警，羌、胡出寇，三府舉能，遷旻匈奴中郎將。

translations.literal: When the frontier alarmed and Qiang and Hu raided, the Three Offices promoted men of ability and named Min Colonel of the Northern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Border raids by Qiang and Hu led the court to post him as colonel against the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 討賊有功，徵拜議郎，還京​​師。

translations.literal: He punished bandits with distinction, was called to the capital as Counsellor, and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Successful campaigns earned him the counsellor's seal and a seat at court.

sentences.zh: 見太尉袁逢，逢問其西域諸國土地、風俗、人物、種數。

translations.literal: He audience with Grand Commandant Yuan Feng; Feng questioned him on every Western Region state's terrain, customs, population, and classification.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yuan Feng interviewed him on the Western Regions—lands, peoples, and customs.

sentences.zh: 旻具答言西域本三十六國，後分為五十五，稍散至百餘國；

translations.literal: Min answered in full that the west originally counted thirty-six states, later split to fifty-five, and ultimately scattered past a hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Min traced how thirty-six Tarim states had fractured into well over a hundred polities;

sentences.zh: 其國大小，道裡近遠，人數多少，風俗燥濕，山川、草木、鳥獸、異物名種，不與中國同者，悉口陳其狀，手畫地形。

translations.literal: for each state's size, mileage, population, climate, mountains, rivers, plants, animals, birds, beasts, and exotic species—all unlike the Middle Kingdom—he gave oral descriptions and sketched maps by hand.
translations.idiomatic: he rehearsed distances, populations, climates, and strange flora and fauna, sketching each kingdom from memory.

sentences.zh: 逢奇其才，嘆息言：「雖班固作西域傳，何以加此？

translations.literal: Feng marveled at his talent and sighed: 'Even Ban Gu's Treatise on the Western Regions could hardly surpass this.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Feng declared Ban Gu's Han essay second to Zang Min's briefing.

sentences.zh: 」旻轉拜長水校尉，終太原太守。〉

translations.literal: Min was transferred to Colonel of the Long River Barracks and ended his career as Administrator of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He closed his career as colonel of the Chang River corps and governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 洪體貌魁梧，有異於人，舉孝廉為郎。

translations.literal: Hong was tall and imposing—no ordinary frame—and entered court as a Gentleman on a Filial and Incorrupt nomination.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong's stature turned heads; the Filial and Incorrupt nomination brought him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時選三署郎以補縣長；

translations.literal: At that time gentlemen of the three palaces were rotated into county magistracies;
translations.idiomatic: The court seconded palace cadets to county posts;

sentences.zh: 琅邪趙昱為莒長，東萊劉繇下邑長，東海王朗菑丘長，洪即丘長。

translations.literal: Zhao Yu of Langya became chief of Ju, Liu Yao of Donglai chief of Xiayi, Wang Lang of Donghai chief of Zaiqiu, and Hong chief of Jiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Peers included Zhao Yu at Ju, Liu Yao at Xiayi, Wang Lang at Zaiqiu, and Zang Hong at Jiqiu.

sentences.zh: 靈帝末，棄官還家，太守張超請洪為功曹。

translations.literal: Late in Emperor Ling's reign he resigned and went home; Administrator Zhang Chao appointed him merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He left office under Ling and served Zhang Chao of Guangling as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 董卓殺帝，圖危社稷，洪說超曰：「明府歷世受恩，兄弟並據大郡，今王室將危，賊臣未梟，此誠天下義烈報恩效命之秋也。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo murdered the sovereign and menaced the dynastic altars, Hong urged Zhang Chao: 'Your house has received generations of favor; you and your brothers hold great commanderies; the throne totters and the traitor still lives—this is the hour for every loyal man to repay his debt.'
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong warned Zhang Chao that Dong Zhuo's crime demanded action while the Han still lived.

sentences.zh: 今郡境尚全，吏民殷富，若動枹鼓，可得二萬人，以此誅除國賊，為天下倡先，義之大者也。

translations.literal: 'Your territory remains intact and your people prosperous—beat the drums and twenty thousand men will answer; strike the Usurper first and you lead the righteous lords of the realm—that is the highest duty.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Raise your district and you can field twenty thousand—kill Dong Zhuo and you shame every warlord who waits.'

sentences.zh: 」超然其言，與洪西至陳留，見兄邈計事。

translations.literal: Chao approved; he and Hong rode west to Chenliu to join Zhang Miao's council.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao agreed and rode with Zang Hong to plan with Zhang Miao at Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 邈亦素有心，會於酸棗，邈謂超曰：「聞弟為郡守，政教威恩，不由己出，動任臧洪，洪者何人？

translations.literal: Miao had long nursed the same purpose; they met at Suanzao. Miao asked Zhang Chao: 'They say you govern your commandery yet every decree passes through Zang Hong—who is he?'
translations.idiomatic: At Suanzao Zhang Miao asked why Zhang Chao let Zang Hong run his administration.

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「洪才略智數優超，超甚愛之，海內奇士也。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao said: 'Hong's gifts outrank mine—I love him—he is a prodigy of our age.'
translations.idiomatic: 'He outclasses me,' said Zhang Chao; 'the realm rarely sees his like.'

sentences.zh: 」邈即引見洪，與語大異之。

translations.literal: Miao received Hong at once and, hearing him speak, knew he was extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: One conversation convinced Zhang Miao.

sentences.zh: 致之於劉兗州公山、孔豫州公緒，皆與洪親善。

translations.literal: He introduced him to Liu Dai of Yanzhou and Kong Zhou of Yuzhou; both befriended Hong warmly.
translations.idiomatic: He presented Zang Hong to Liu Dai and Kong Zhou, who embraced him.

sentences.zh: 乃設壇場，方共盟誓，諸州郡更相讓，莫敢當，咸共推洪。

translations.literal: They raised an altar and deferred the oath until every prefecture refused the honor—all thrust Zang Hong forward.
translations.idiomatic: They built a covenant altar; every lord declined leadership until Zang Hong alone remained.

sentences.zh: 洪乃升壇操槃歃血而盟曰：「漢室不幸，皇綱失統，賊臣董卓乘釁縱害，禍加至尊，虐流百姓，大懼淪喪社稷，翦覆四海。

translations.literal: Hong mounted the altar, lifted the sacrificial cup, smeared blood, and swore: 'The Han starves—imperial rule frays; Dong Zhuo exploits turmoil to wound the Son of Heaven and scourge the people; we dread the altars will fall and the realm burn.'
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong's oath condemned Dong Zhuo for rending heaven's net and threatening the temples of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史岱、豫州刺史伷、陳留太守邈、東郡太守瑁、廣陵太守超等，糾合義兵，並赴國難。

translations.literal: Inspectors Liu Dai of Yanzhou and Zhou of Yuzhou, Administrators Zhang Miao of Chenliu, Mao of Dongjun, Zhang Chao of Guangling, and others rally righteous hosts to the nation's peril.'
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou, Yuzhou, Chenliu, Dongjun, and Guangling pledged arms for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 凡我同盟，齊心戮力，以致臣節，殞首喪元，必無二志。

translations.literal: 'All who share this bond shall unite in loyal service—heads may roll, hearts never waver.'
translations.idiomatic: 'We vow one purpose—to restore the Han or die.'

sentences.zh: 有渝此盟，俾墜其命，無克遺育。

translations.literal: 'Whoever breaks this oath—may line and offspring perish.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Break faith and lose posterity.'

sentences.zh: 皇天后土，祖宗明靈，實皆鑑之！

translations.literal: 'Heaven above, earth below, spirits of our ancestors—bear witness!'
translations.idiomatic: 'Let Heaven, earth, and our fathers judge us!'

sentences.zh: 」洪辭氣慷慨，涕泣橫下，聞其言者，雖卒伍廝養，莫不激揚，人思致節。

translations.literal: Hong spoke with tears streaming; even camp servants burned to prove themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His voice shook the altar—even grooms swore themselves to the cause.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：於時此盟止有劉岱等五人而已。

translations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi notes: only five men such as Liu Dai stood at that oath.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi: the roster held barely five signatories—Liu Dai among them.

sentences.zh: 魏氏春秋橫內劉表等數人，皆非事實。

translations.literal: The Wei Chronicle wrongly inserts Liu Biao and others.
translations.idiomatic: Later editors padded the list with Liu Biao—without evidence.

sentences.zh: 表保據江、漢，身未嘗出境，何由得與洪同壇而盟乎？〉

translations.literal: Biao held Jiang and Han without leaving his borders—how could he have sworn with Hong?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao never left Jing—he could not have shared Zang Hong's altar.

sentences.zh: 頃之，諸軍莫適先進，而食盡眾散。

translations.literal: Soon no army would march first; grain ran out and the coalition scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Stalemate starved the alliance apart.

sentences.zh: 超遣洪詣大司馬劉虞謀，值公孫瓚之難，至河間，遇幽、冀二州交兵，使命不達。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao sent Hong to Grand Marshal Liu Yu; Gongsun Zan's coup blocked the road at Hejian—You and Ji were at war and the embassy failed.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong never reached Liu Yu—Hejian was a battlefield.

sentences.zh: 而袁紹見洪，又奇重之，與結分合好。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan Shao received Hong with awe and won his friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao admired him and sealed a personal tie.

sentences.zh: 會青州刺史焦和卒，紹使洪領青州以撫其眾。

translations.literal: When Qingzhou's governor Jiao He died, Shao put Hong in charge to calm the province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao named him acting Qingzhou governor after Jiao He's death.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：初平中，焦和為青​​州刺史。

translations.literal: The Jiuzhou Chunqiu says: during Chuping Jiao He governed Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of the Nine Provinces opens with Jiao He's tenure.

sentences.zh: 是時英雄並起，黃巾寇暴，和務及同盟，俱入京畿，不暇為民保障，引軍逾河而西。

translations.literal: Heroes rose everywhere; Yellow Turbans ravaged the land; He chased alliance duty into the capital plain and left Qingzhou undefended, marching west across the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao He rushed east to the coalition, abandoning Qingzhou to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 未久而袁、曹二公卓將戰於滎陽，敗績。

translations.literal: Soon Yuan and Cao clashed at Xingyang and broke.
translations.idiomatic: The lords lost at Xingyang almost immediately.

sentences.zh: 黃巾遂廣，屠裂城邑。

translations.literal: The Turbans spread, sacking towns.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels overran the province.

sentences.zh: 和不能禦，然軍器尚利，戰士尚眾，而耳目偵邏不設，恐動之言妄至，望寇奔走，未嘗接風塵交旗鼓也。

translations.literal: He could not stop them; arms and men remained, yet he posted no scouts—rumor routed him before an arrow flew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao He kept sharp blades and full ranks but no intelligence—panic scattered his host unseen.

sentences.zh: 欲作陷冰丸沈河，令賊不得渡，禱祈群神，求用兵必利，耆筮常陳於前，巫祝不去於側；

translations.literal: He tried sinking ice balls to block fords, prayed to every god for victory, stacked yarrow stalks, and kept shamans at his elbow;
translations.idiomatic: He tried freezing the river with weighted balls, stuffed his tent with oracles and witches,

sentences.zh: 入見其清談干雲，出則渾亂，命不可知。

translations.literal: eloquent in council, chaotic in the field—fate unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: brilliant in talk, helpless in war.

sentences.zh: 州遂蕭條，悉為丘墟也。〉

translations.literal: The province turned waste—ashes and rubble.'
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou became a wasteland.'

sentences.zh: 洪在州二年，群盜奔走。

translations.literal: Hong governed two years and drove every band away.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong cleared the province in twenty-four months.

sentences.zh: 紹歎其能，徙為東郡太守，治東武陽。

translations.literal: Shao praised his gift and moved him to Administrator of Dongjun at Dongwuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao transferred him to Dongjun with seat at Dongwuyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖圍張超於雍丘，超言：「唯恃臧洪，當來救吾。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor besieged Zhang Chao at Yongqiu; Chao said: 'I trust only Zang Hong—he must rescue me.'
translations.idiomatic: At Yongqiu Zhang Chao pinned hope on Zang Hong.

sentences.zh: 」眾人以為袁、曹方睦，而洪為紹所表用，必不敗好招禍，遠來赴此。

translations.literal: Others argued Yuan and Cao were allied and Hong owed Yuan Shao—surely he would not wreck that tie for a distant friend.
translations.idiomatic: Skeptics said Yuan Shao would never let Zang Hong march against Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 超曰：「子源，天下義士，終不背本者，但恐見禁制，不相及逮耳。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao said: 'Ziyuan is righteousness itself—he will not forsake roots—only Yuan Shao may chain him too late.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Zang Hong keeps faith,' Zhang Chao insisted—unless Yuan Shao forbids him.

sentences.zh: 」洪聞之，果徒跣號泣，並勒所領兵，又從紹請兵馬，求欲救超，而紹終不聽許。

translations.literal: Hong heard, went barefoot wailing, mustered his command, begged Yuan Shao for troops—and Shao refused to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong wept barefoot and begged Yuan Shao for relief; Yuan Shao said no.

sentences.zh: 超遂族滅。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao's line was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao's house died to the last.

sentences.zh: 洪由是怨紹，絕不與通。

translations.literal: Hong therefore hated Shao and broke off all ties.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong renounced Yuan Shao forever.

sentences.zh: 紹興兵圍之，歷年不下。

translations.literal: Shao raised armies and besieged him for years without success.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao besieged Dongwuyang for years.

sentences.zh: 紹令洪邑人陳琳書與洪，喻以禍福，責以恩義。

translations.literal: Shao had townsman Chen Lin write: fortune, disaster, obligation—everything pressed on Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao ordered Chen Lin's letter of appeal and threat.

sentences.zh: 洪答曰：

translations.literal: Hong answered:
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong wrote back:

sentences.zh: 隔闊相思，發於寤寐。

translations.literal: Long apart—longing wakes and sleeps with me.
translations.idiomatic: Separation haunts my dreams.

sentences.zh: 幸相去步武之間耳，而以趣舍異規，不得相見，其為愴悢，可為心哉！

translations.literal: We stand only paces apart yet choices divide us—what ache is deeper?
translations.idiomatic: We are neighbors in principle yet worlds apart—how bitter.

sentences.zh: 前日不遺，比辱雅貺，述敘禍福，公私切至。

translations.literal: You honored me lately with a letter weighing blessing and curse—public and private both knife-sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Your recent letter laid out doom and duty with brutal clarity.

sentences.zh: 所以不即奉答者，既學薄才鈍，不足塞詰；

translations.literal: I delayed reply because my learning is thin and tongue slow—too weak to answer point by point;
translations.idiomatic: I lacked wit to match your rhetoric;

sentences.zh: 亦以吾子攜負側室，息肩主人，家在東州，僕為仇敵。

translations.literal: and because you nest your concubine beside your patron while your kin live east—I am your master's sworn foe.
translations.idiomatic: and because you serve Yuan Shao who wars on my lord while your family stays in the east.

sentences.zh: 以是事人，雖披中情，墮肝膽，猶身疏有罪，言甘見怪，方首尾不救，何能卹人？

translations.literal: To plead with such a patron—even baring soul and liver—I remain the guilty exile; sweet phrases still sound false; I cannot save myself—how pity you?
translations.idiomatic: Even heartfelt pleas would sound like treason from Zang Hong—how could I counsel you?

sentences.zh: 且以子之才，窮該典籍，豈將闇於大道，不達餘趣哉！

translations.literal: With your erudition you cannot miss the Great Way's drift—surely!
translations.idiomatic: You know the canon—can you truly misunderstand?

sentences.zh: 然猶復云云者，僕以是知足下之言，信不由衷，將以救禍也。

translations.literal: Yet you repeat yourself—I infer your words are not sincere but meant to spare yourself disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Your speech aims at self-preservation, not truth.

sentences.zh: 必欲算計長短，辯諮是非，是非之論，言滿天下，陳之更不明，不言無所損。

translations.literal: If we tally every grievance the world already brims with debate—speaking clarifies nothing, silence costs nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Rehashing old scores helps neither of us.

sentences.zh: 又言傷告絕之義，非吾所忍行也，是以捐棄紙筆，一無所答。

translations.literal: To answer would stain the severance I proclaimed—I dropped brush and ink entirely.
translations.idiomatic: I stayed silent to honor our break.

sentences.zh: 亦冀遙忖其心，知其計定，不復渝變也。

translations.literal: I hoped distance would show you my resolve—fixed, irreversible.
translations.idiomatic: I thought my silence stated my final word.

sentences.zh: 重獲來命，援引古今，紛紜六紙，雖慾不言，焉得已哉！

translations.literal: Your second letter fills six pages of precedent—I can keep quiet no longer.
translations.idiomatic: Your new six-page brief forces my pen.

sentences.zh: 僕小人也，本因行役，寇竊大州，恩深分厚，寧樂今日自還接刃！

translations.literal: I am a petty officer who seized a great province by chance; your kindness ran deep—would I trade blades with joy today?
translations.idiomatic: I owe Yuan Shao much yet we draw swords—think what that costs me.

sentences.zh: 每登城勒兵，望主人之旗鼓，感故友之周旋，撫弦搦矢，不覺流涕之覆面也。

translations.literal: Each time I man the walls and see my old master's banners I touch bowstring and weep.
translations.idiomatic: On the parapet I see your drums and weep like a child.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 自以輔佐主人，無以為悔。

translations.literal: I thought serving my lord left nothing to regret.
translations.idiomatic: I believed serving Yuan Shao blameless.

sentences.zh: 主人相接，過絕等倫。

translations.literal: His favor passed every measure.
translations.idiomatic: His grace knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 當受任之初，自謂究竟大事，共尊王室。

translations.literal: When first commissioned I meant to finish the great work and honor the Son of Heaven together.
translations.idiomatic: We meant to restore the Han together.

sentences.zh: 豈悟天子不悅，本州見侵，郡將遘牖里之厄，陳留克創兵之謀，謀計棲遲，喪忠孝之名，杖策攜背，虧交友之分。

translations.literal: Who foresaw the emperor's wrath, my province invaded, my patron trapped like King Wen of Shang, Chenliu plotting arms—plans stalled, loyalty and filial piety lost, friendship betrayed by the whip I leaned on?
translations.idiomatic: Instead the throne turned hostile, my home fell, Zhang Miao died at Yongqiu, and Chenliu armed itself—I lost honor as son and friend alike.

sentences.zh: 揆此二者，與其不得已，喪忠孝之名與虧交友之道，輕重殊塗，親疏異畫，故便收淚告絕。

translations.literal: Weighing ruin—whether to lose loyal names or break friendship—kin and weight differ; therefore I wiped tears and declared our friendship dead.
translations.idiomatic: Forced to choose, I chose integrity over fond memory.

sentences.zh: 若使主人少垂故人，住者側席，去者克己，不汲汲於離友，信刑戮以自輔，則僕抗季札之志，不為今日之戰矣。

translations.literal: Had my lord spared old ties—guests adjusting mats, leavers restraining pride—not rushed to slaughter friends, I would show Jizi's forbearance and we would not fight today.
translations.idiomatic: Had Yuan Shao shown mercy, I would keep Guan Zhong's patience—no siege between us.

sentences.zh: 何以效之？

translations.literal: How prove it?
translations.idiomatic: Proof?

sentences.zh: 昔張景明親登壇啖血，奉辭奔走，卒使韓牧讓印，主人得地；

translations.literal: Zhang Jingming once mounted the altar, sucked blood, ran Yuan Shao's errands until Han Fu yielded Ji and your lord took the province;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingming sealed the alliance, rushed Han Fu's abdication, and won you Ji Province;

sentences.zh: 然後但以拜章朝主，賜爵獲傳之故，旋時之間，不蒙觀過之貸，而受夷滅之禍。

translations.literal: yet a memorial and patent later bought him no mercy—annihilation in an eyeblink.
translations.idiomatic: a court memorial earned him execution overnight.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案《英雄記》云：「袁紹使張景明、郭公則、高元才等說韓馥，使讓冀州。

translations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi notes the Yingxiong ji: Yuan Shao sent Zhang Jingming, Guo Gongze, and Gao Yuancai to persuade Han Fu to yield Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Pei cites the Record of Heroes on Zhang Jingming's embassy to Han Fu.

sentences.zh: 」然馥之讓位，景明亦有其功。

translations.literal: Fu's abdication owed Jingming part of the credit.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu's surrender owed Zhang Jingming effort.

sentences.zh: 其餘之事未詳。〉

translations.literal: The rest lacks detail.'
translations.idiomatic: Pei leaves the rest obscure.'

sentences.zh: 呂奉先討卓來奔，請兵不獲，告去何罪？

translations.literal: Lü Fengxian campaigned against Dong Zhuo and fled here; he begged for troops and obtained none—what crime lay in announcing his departure?
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fled from Dong Zhuo, asked you for aid, got none, and left—where was the offense?

sentences.zh: 復見斫刺，濱於死亡。

translations.literal: Again he was hacked and stabbed—he brushed death.
translations.idiomatic: You hunted him again until he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 劉子琪奉使逾時，辭不獲命，畏威懷親，以詐求歸，可謂有志忠孝，無損霸道者也；

translations.literal: Liu Ziqi bore his commission past its term; refusal was impossible—he feared your wrath yet longed for kin and sought home by stratagem—call him loyal and filial, no threat to ambition;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ziqi overstayed his embassy, could not resign, feigned a way home for family's sake—loyal son, no rival to your power—

sentences.zh: 然輒僵斃麾下，不蒙虧除。

translations.literal: Yet suddenly he lay dead among his lord's men, granted no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: yet you struck him down without mercy.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：公孫瓚表列紹罪過雲：「紹與故虎牙將軍劉勛首共造兵，勳仍有效，而以小忿枉害於勳，紹罪七也。

translations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi notes: Gongsun Zan's memorial listing Yuan Shao's crimes states: 'Shao together with the former Tiger-Fang general Liu Xun jointly raised troops; Xun still had merit, yet over a petty grudge Shao unjustly killed Xun—this is Shao's seventh crime.'
translations.idiomatic: Pei cites Gongsun Zan's indictment: Yuan Shao murdered the veteran general Liu Xun over a private spite—the seventh count.

sentences.zh: 」疑此是子璜也。〉

translations.literal: I suspect this refers to Zihuang.'
translations.idiomatic: Pei identifies him with Liu Zihuang.'

sentences.zh: 僕雖不敏，又素不能原始見終，睹微知著，竊度主人之心，豈謂三子宜死，罰當刑中哉？

translations.literal: Though I am dull and never trace origins to outcomes or infer the large from the small, I privately measure my lord's heart—did he truly judge those three deserved death and punishment fit the crime?
translations.idiomatic: I am slow-witted, yet I doubt Yuan Shao thought those men deserved execution.

sentences.zh: 實且欲一統山東，增兵討讎，懼戰士狐疑，無以沮勸，故抑廢王命以崇承製，慕義者蒙榮，待放者被戮，此乃主人之利，非遊士之原也。

translations.literal: In truth he wished to unify the east of the mountains, swell his host to avenge slights, yet feared his soldiers would waver with nothing to daunt or encourage—therefore he suppressed the king's mandate to exalt his own orders, honored followers and slaughtered the reluctant—that served his interest, not a wandering scholar's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to dominate Shandong and cow his army by branding imperial orders—rewarding friends and killing doubters.

sentences.zh: 故僕鑑戒前人，困窮死戰。

translations.literal: Therefore I take warning from past victims and fight to the death in straits.
translations.idiomatic: So I learned from their fate and fight on though trapped.

sentences.zh: 僕雖下愚，亦嘗聞君子之言矣。

translations.literal: Though I am base foolishness, I too have heard what gentlemen say.
translations.idiomatic: Even a dullard hears the sages.

sentences.zh: 此實非吾心也。

translations.literal: This truly is not my heart.
translations.idiomatic: That was never my wish.

sentences.zh: 乃主人招焉。

translations.literal: It was the lord who summoned me.
translations.idiomatic: Your master drew me in.

sentences.zh: 凡吾所以背棄國民，用命此城者，正以君子之違，不適敵國故也。

translations.literal: All my reason for abandoning your people and staking my life on this wall is that a gentleman's breach does not reach the enemy state.
translations.idiomatic: I hold this city because honor forbids me to serve your rival.

sentences.zh: 是以獲罪主人，見攻逾時，而足下更引此義以為吾規，無乃辭同趨異，非君子所為休戚者哉！

translations.literal: Therefore I earned my lord's offense and have been attacked all this while—yet you cite that very principle to lecture me—is this not the same words with opposite intent, unworthy of a gentleman's shared joy and grief?
translations.idiomatic: You twist the code that drove my breach—hardly the conduct of a friend.

sentences.zh: 吾聞之也，義不背親，忠不違君，故東宗本州以為親援，中扶郡將以安社稷，一舉二得以徼忠孝，何以為非？

translations.literal: I have heard: righteousness does not betray kin, loyalty does not defy the ruler—therefore I honor my home province as kin and uphold my governor to steady the altars; one stroke serves both loyalty and filial piety—how is that wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Righteous men honor kin and sovereign—I aid my province and my patron together.

sentences.zh: 而足下欲吾輕本破家，均君主人。

translations.literal: Yet you would have me wreck home and kin to equate with your master.
translations.idiomatic: You ask me to destroy my roots to match Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 主人之於我也，年為吾兄，分為篤友，道乖告去，以安君親，可謂順矣。

translations.literal: My patron has been my elder brother in years and my steadfast friend in duty—when ways diverged I left to save kin and lord alike—may that be called fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When paths split I withdrew to protect family and lord—that was order.

sentences.zh: 若子之言，則包胥宜致命於伍員，不當號哭於秦庭矣。

translations.literal: By your logic Shen Baoxu should have died for Wu Yuan instead of weeping in Qin's court.
translations.idiomatic: Your rule would make Shen Baoxu stab Wu Zixu rather than wail at Qin.

sentences.zh: 苟區區於攘患，不知言乖乎道理矣。

translations.literal: If one fusses only over removing peril one no longer speaks with reason.
translations.idiomatic: Pedantic rescue misses the moral point.

sentences.zh: 足下或者見城圍不解，救兵未至，感婚姻之義，惟平生之好，以屈節而苟生，勝守義而傾覆也。

translations.literal: Perhaps you see the siege unlifted and relief absent—moved by marriage ties and old friendship—think bending the knee for life beats holding righteousness to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps you think marriage and old ties should make me yield rather than die upright.

sentences.zh: 昔晏嬰不降志於白刃，南史不曲筆以求生，故身著圖像，名垂後世，況僕據金城之固，驅士民之力，散三年之畜，以為一年之資，匡困補乏，以悅天下，何圖築室反耕哉！

translations.literal: Formerly Yan Ying did not bend his will before naked blades; the southern scribe would not twist his brush to live—therefore his portrait endures and his name lasts—how much more I hold firm walls, drive people of substance, spend three years' stores as one year's supply, aid the needy and please the realm—why plot stockades and fallow fields!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying defied swords; the Qi chronicler chose death—posterity remembers them. I hold strong walls, willing arms, stores for a year's siege—why talk of long fortification?

sentences.zh: 但懼秋風揚塵，伯珪馬首南向，張楊、飛燕，膂力作難，北鄙將告倒縣之急，股肱奏乞歸之誠耳。

translations.literal: I only fear autumn wind raising dust—Bogui's cavalry wheeling south; Zhang Yang and the Feiyan band flexing sinews to strike north—the frontier will cry inverted-hanging distress while your arm ministers beg leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn may bring Gongsun Zan south, Zhang Yang and Heishan in arms—your northern flank could panic while your courtiers flee homeward.

sentences.zh: 主人當鑑我曹輩，反旌退師，治兵鄴垣，何宜久辱盛怒，暴威於吾城下哉？

translations.literal: Let my lord take warning from us, wheel his banners homeward, drill his men at Ye's wall—why prolong wrath and thunder at my ramparts?
translations.idiomatic: Take your lesson, withdraw to Ye, train your host—why waste fury on my stones?

sentences.zh: 足下譏吾恃黑山以為救，獨不念黃巾之合從邪！

translations.literal: You mock me for trusting Heishan for rescue—have you forgotten the Yellow Turbans' league?
translations.idiomatic: You jeer at Heishan allies—did Yuan Shao scorn the Turbans' coalition?

sentences.zh: 加飛燕之屬悉以受王命矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Feiyan sorts all received royal commission.
translations.idiomatic: Even Feiyan bands hold imperial warrant now.

sentences.zh: 昔高祖取彭越於鉅野，光武創基兆於綠林，卒能龍飛中興，以成帝業，苟可輔主興化，夫何嫌哉！

translations.literal: Gaozu recruited Peng Yue from Juye; Guangwu founded his rise from the Green Woods—both flew as dragons and restored the house—if one can aid the sovereign and renew the teaching, what shame attaches?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu took Peng Yue from bandits; Guangwu rose through Green Woods—virtue sanctifies the source.

sentences.zh: 況僕親奉璽書，與之從事。

translations.literal: How much more I personally bore the seal-script edict and served beside them.
translations.idiomatic: I serve them under imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 行矣孔璋！

translations.literal: Enough, Kongzhang!
translations.idiomatic: Farewell, Chen Lin.

sentences.zh: 足下徼利於境外，臧洪授命於君親；

translations.literal: You chase profit beyond the border; Zang Hong spends life for lord and kin.
translations.idiomatic: You hunt gain abroad; I die for patron and family.

sentences.zh: 吾子託身於盟主，臧洪策名於長安。

translations.literal: You lodge with the covenant chief; Zang Hong pledged name at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: You cling to the warlord; I swore fealty at the capital.

sentences.zh: 子謂餘身死而名滅，僕亦笑子生死而無聞焉，悲哉！

translations.literal: You say my death erases my name—I laugh that your life and death will leave no echo—how sad!
translations.idiomatic: You predict my oblivion—your own tale may vanish first.

sentences.zh: 本同而末離，努力努力，夫復何言！

translations.literal: We began together yet end apart—strive on—what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: We started as one road and forked—take care—there is nothing left to say.

sentences.zh: 紹見洪書，知無降意，增兵急攻。

translations.literal: When Shao read Hong's letter and knew there would be no surrender, he increased troops and attacked fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Zang Hong's refusal, Yuan Shao doubled the assault.

sentences.zh: 城中糧穀以盡，外無強救，洪自度必不免，呼吏士謂曰：「袁氏無道，所圖不軌，且不救洪郡將。

translations.literal: Grain inside the city was exhausted and no strong relief came without; Hong reckoned he could not escape and called clerks and soldiers, saying: 'The Yuan clan is lawless, plots rebellion, and would not save my governor.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies failed Zang Hong told his men the Yuans were traitors who let Zhang Chao die.

sentences.zh: 洪於大義，不得不死，今諸君無事空與此禍！

translations.literal: Hong by great righteousness must die—why should you all suffer this calamity for nothing!'
translations.idiomatic: I die for honor—you need not share my doom.'

sentences.zh: 可先城未敗，將妻子出。

translations.literal: Before the walls fall take wives and children out.'
translations.idiomatic: Send your families out while you can.'

sentences.zh: 」將吏士民皆垂泣曰：「明府與袁氏本無怨隙，今為本朝郡將之故，自致殘困，吏民何忍當舍明府去也！

translations.literal: Officers, soldiers, and people all wept: 'You had no feud with the Yuans—you ruin yourself for the court's governor—how could we abandon you!'
translations.idiomatic: The garrison wept that he fought for Han while clean of private spite—they would not leave.

sentences.zh: 」初尚掘鼠煮筋角，後無可複食者。

translations.literal: At first they still dug rats and boiled horn and sinew; afterward nothing remained to eat again.
translations.idiomatic: They ate rats and leather until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 主簿啟內廚米三鬥，請中分稍以為糜粥，洪歎曰：「獨食此何為！

translations.literal: The chief clerk reported three dou of inner-kitchen rice and begged to halve it for thin gruel; Hong sighed: 'To eat this alone—what for!'
translations.idiomatic: Three dou of rice reached the clerk's desk; Zang Hong refused private bowls.

sentences.zh: 」使作薄粥，眾分歠之，殺其愛妾以食將士。

translations.literal: He had thin gruel made for all to sip and slew his beloved concubine to feed the officers.
translations.idiomatic: He shared watery gruel and killed his favorite concubine for the troops.

sentences.zh: 將士咸流涕，無能仰視者。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers all wept—none could lift eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Men sobbed too hard to look up.

sentences.zh: 男女七八千人相枕而死，莫有離叛。

translations.literal: Seven or eight thousand men and women pillow-lapped each other in death—none rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Seven thousand died side by side without desertion.

sentences.zh: 城陷，紹生執洪。

translations.literal: When the city fell Shao captured Hong alive.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao took Zang Hong alive when the walls broke.

sentences.zh: 紹素親洪，盛施幃幔，大會諸將見洪，謂曰：「臧洪，何相負若此！

translations.literal: Shao had always been intimate with Hong; he draped curtains lavishly and assembled generals to meet Hong, saying: 'Zang Hong—how could you betray me thus!'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao, once fond of him, staged a grand tent and demanded why Zang Hong turned.

sentences.zh: 今日服未？

translations.literal: Will you submit today?'
translations.idiomatic: Will you yield now?'

sentences.zh: 」洪據地瞋目曰：「諸袁事漢，四世五公，可謂受恩。

translations.literal: Hong sat on the ground, glaring: 'The Yuans served Han—four generations, five dukes—richly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong glared from the floor: 'Your house enjoyed four generations of Han favor.'

sentences.zh: 今王室衰弱，無扶翼之意，欲因際會，希冀非望，多殺忠良以立姦威。

translations.literal: Now the royal house fails and you mean no aid—you seize the moment to covet what is not yours, slaughtering the loyal to build tyrant awe.
translations.idiomatic: Now you abandon the throne, murder the good, and hunger for the mandate.'

sentences.zh: 洪親見呼張陳留為兄，則洪府君亦宜為弟，同共戮力，為國除害，何為擁眾觀人屠滅！

translations.literal: Hong himself heard you call Administrator Zhang of Chenliu 'elder brother'—then Hong's lord must be younger brother—together we should strike evil for the state—why mass troops and watch men butchered!'
translations.idiomatic: You called Zhang Miao brother—then share duty against rebels instead of watching slaughter.'

sentences.zh: 惜洪力劣，不能推刃為天下報仇，何謂服乎！

translations.literal: It pains Hong that his strength failed—he could not blade you for the realm's revenge—what talk of submission!'
translations.idiomatic: I lack strength to avenge the Han—submission?'

sentences.zh: 」紹本愛洪，意欲令屈服，原之；

translations.literal: Shao had loved Hong and wished to make him yield and forgive;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao wanted him to bend and live;

sentences.zh: 見洪辭切，知終不為己用，乃殺之。

translations.literal: seeing Hong's words harsh, knew he would never serve him—thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: seeing his resolve, executed him.

sentences.zh: 〈徐眾《三國評》曰：洪敦天下名義，救舊君之危，其恩足以感人情，義足以勵薄俗。

translations.literal: Xu Zhong's Critique of the Three Kingdoms says: Hong upheld the realm's right and rescued his former lord—grace enough to move hearts, duty enough to steel the shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhong praises Zang Hong's covenant loyalty.

sentences.zh: 然袁亦知己親友，致位州郡，雖非君臣，且實盟主，既受其命，義不應貳。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan was also intimate friend and patron who raised him to provincial rank—not quite lord and vassal yet truly covenant chief; once he accepted orders he should not have doubled allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuan Shao raised him—accepting command bound him.

sentences.zh: 袁、曹方睦，夾輔王室，呂布反覆無義，志在逆亂，而邈、超擅立布為州牧，其於王法，乃一罪人也。

translations.literal: Yuan and Cao were allied in aiding the royal house; Lü Bu was faithless treason—Zhang Miao and Zhang Chao made him governor—by royal law they were criminals.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao attacked rebels Yuan Shao ignored—Zhang Chao backed Lü Bu against law.

sentences.zh: 曹公討之，袁氏弗救，未為非理也。

translations.literal: Cao attacked them—Yuan offered no succor—not unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao owed Zhang Chao nothing.

sentences.zh: 洪本不當就袁請兵，又不當還為怨讎。

translations.literal: Hong ought not have begged Yuan for troops nor turned enemy afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong should neither have asked Yuan's aid nor blamed him for refusal.

sentences.zh: 為洪計者，苟力所不足，可奔他國以求赴救，若謀力未展以待事機，則宜徐更觀釁，效死於超。

translations.literal: For Hong's planning—if strength fell short he could flee abroad for rescue; if schemes lacked scope he could await occasion—die for Zhang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Better flee for help or die beside Zhang Chao than stubborn siege.

sentences.zh: 何必誓守窮城而無變通，身死殄民，功名不立，良可哀也！〉

translations.literal: Why swear to a doomed town without flexibility—dying, extinguishing the people, winning no fame—pitiful indeed!'
translations.idiomatic: Why waste lives on a hopeless wall?'

sentences.zh: 洪邑人陳容少為書生，親慕洪，隨洪為東郡丞；

translations.literal: Hong's townsman Chen Rong in youth was a scholar-student; he admired Hong and followed him as deputy of Dongjun;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Rong of Donghai revered Zang Hong and served as his aide.

sentences.zh: 城未敗，洪遣出。

translations.literal: before the city fell Hong sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong sent him out before the fall.

sentences.zh: 紹令在坐，見洪當死，起謂紹曰：「將軍舉大事，欲為天下除暴，而專先誅忠義，豈合天意！

translations.literal: Shao ordered him to sit with the assembly; seeing Hong about to die he rose and said to Shao: 'You raise a great enterprise to cleanse the realm—yet you kill loyalty first—does that match Heaven's mind!'
translations.idiomatic: Seated at Yuan Shao's banquet Chen Rong protested the execution.

sentences.zh: 臧洪發舉為郡將，奈何殺之！

translations.literal: Zang Hong raised you to governor—how kill him!'
translations.idiomatic: You owe him your rank—how murder him?'

sentences.zh: 」紹慚，左右使人牽出，謂曰：「汝非臧洪儔，空复爾為！

translations.literal: Shao flushed and attendants dragged him forth; Shao said: 'You are no peer of Zang Hong—why this empty gesture!'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao reddened and sneered that Chen Rong was no Zang Hong.

sentences.zh: 」容顧曰：「夫仁義豈有常，蹈之則君子，背之則小人。

translations.literal: Rong looked back: 'Are benevolence and righteousness fixed—walk them and you are a gentleman; betray them and you are petty.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Rong answered that honor defines the man.

sentences.zh: 今日寧與臧洪同日而死，不與將軍同日而生！

translations.literal: Today I would die the same day as Zang Hong—not live your lord's day!'
translations.idiomatic: Better die with Zang Hong than live under you.'

sentences.zh: 」復見殺。

translations.literal: Again he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: They executed Chen Rong too.

sentences.zh: 在紹坐者無不嘆息，竊相謂曰：「如何一日殺二烈士！

translations.literal: None seated with Shao did not sigh and whisper: 'How kill two martyrs in one day!'
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses muttered at two righteous deaths in a dawn.

sentences.zh: 」先是，洪遣司馬二人出，求救於呂布；

translations.literal: Earlier Hong had sent two majors out to beg rescue from Lü Bu;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong had dispatched two aides to Lü Bu;

sentences.zh: 比還，城已陷，皆赴敵死。

translations.literal: when they returned the city had fallen—both charged the foe and died.
translations.idiomatic: they returned too late and died charging Yuan's lines.

sentences.zh: 作者評價

translations.literal: Author's commentary
translations.idiomatic: Editorial comment

sentences.zh: 評曰：呂布有虓虎之勇，而無英奇之略，輕狡反覆，唯利是視。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Lü Bu had tiger-like ferocity but no heroic stratagem—light, treacherous, and faithless, seeing only profit.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Lü Bu fought like a tiger yet lacked judgment—faithless and greedy.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，未有若此不夷滅也。

translations.literal: From antiquity to now none such avoid annihilation.
translations.idiomatic: Such men never escape ruin.

sentences.zh: 昔漢光武謬於龐萌，近魏太祖亦蔽於張邈。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Guangwu erred over Pang Meng; lately Wei Taizu was blinded by Zhang Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu misread Pang Meng; Cao Cao misjudged Zhang Miao.

sentences.zh: 知人則哲，唯帝難之，信矣！

translations.literal: To know men is wisdom—only for the sovereign is it hard—indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Knowing men is sage kings' hardest art.

sentences.zh: 陳登、臧洪並有雄氣壯節，登降年夙隕，功業未遂，洪以兵弱敵強，烈志不立，惜哉！

translations.literal: Chen Deng and Zang Hong both possessed heroic spirit and steadfast integrity—Deng died young before deeds were done; Hong faced stronger foes with weaker arms—his blazing aim unfulfilled—pitiful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng and Zang Hong burned bright—one died young, one outmatched—both unfinished tragedies.
